## Step P2-10c′-homologdb — 2026-07-26: the model-independent homolog-search target-DB builder + SLURM sbatch (ADR-0006 D7 + A1; authored to the §9.3 submit-ack)

**Inputs.** ADR-0006 **D7** (the homolog set is assembled by a model-independent sequence-homology search — nhmmer / BLAST / cmsearch-from-candidate — not model-grouped membership; inclusion thresholds P6-frozen, D17) + **A1** (the target that search runs against: the 2,500 GTDB R232 species reps); the fetched genomes `data/interim/production_genomes/<acc>.fna` (2,500 `.fna`, DVC md5 `0d477f38…dir`, `total_bp 7,023,377,857`, P2-10c′-fetch job 739); the git-frozen per-genome integrity baseline `data/processed/audits/production_windows_report.json` (`per_genome[{assembly_accession,n_contigs,total_bp}]`, 2,500 genomes, `total_bp 7,023,377,857`, P2-10c′-shardspec); `envs/homology.yml` + `envs/homology.conda-lock.yml` (hmmer **3.4** → `nhmmer`/`makehmmerdb`, blast **2.17.0** → `makeblastdb`/`blastdbcmd`/`blastn`, biopython — **no infernal, no pandas**; ADR-0002 A12); the reused `pilot_fetch.{iter_fasta_records,normalize_fasta,FASTA_WRAP}` + `provenance.write_provenance`. **Process.** Authored the **homolog-DB build** — the last-but-one of the four-piece P2-10c′ machinery gap (manifest g ✓ → fetch ✓ → shard-spec emitter ✓ → **this** / fetched-window→negative path). New `mining/homolog_db.py` is torch-free **and** pandas-free (the tbox-homology env has neither): the frozen accession set + per-genome baseline are read from the stdlib-JSON window-count report, never the parquet; `pilot_fetch`'s reader is pandas-free at import so it is reused (the genome-FASTA read + `<accession>:c<contig_index>` naming inlined to keep window_dataset's numpy/torch out of the import graph). It concatenates the 2,500 FASTAs into one header-rewritten **target FASTA** (contig ids `<accession>:c<ci>`, the `substrate_windows.window_name` contig scheme so every hit traces to its source genome), then builds a `makeblastdb` **nucleotide DB** + a `makehmmerdb` **FM-index** — the three D7 routes' targets (blastn→BLAST DB; nhmmer→FM-index or plain FASTA; cmsearch-from-candidate→FASTA). Certification is **not** "files exist": a **two-independent-reads integrity** check (the concatenation re-measures every genome's contig/bp and asserts equality to the git-frozen baseline; `blastdbcmd -info` cross-checked against the same concatenated totals) plus a **must-fire round-trip control** — a real 500-nt sub-sequence of the **first and last** accession-sorted genome must self-recover **at its own `<accession>:c<ci>`** by `blastn` (pident ≥ 99, E ≤ 1e-5) **and** `nhmmer`; probing both ends catches a truncated concatenation, and identity (not hit-count) is asserted so a hit at the wrong genome is refused ([[symmetric-count-fixture-blind-to-inversion]]). Tool versions are asserted where they run (blast 2.17.0, hmmer 3.4 — the A11 lesson). `slurm/p2/build_homolog_db.sbatch` is a **single CPU-only job on the `gpu` partition** (no `--gres`/`--array`/`--nodelist`), env `tbox-homology` (created once on the cluster from the pinned lock, `conda-lock install --name tbox-homology envs/homology.conda-lock.yml` — the [[cluster-has-no-tbox-data-env]] gap); it reads the genomes already on the cluster from job 739 (no staging), builds in node-local `/tmp`, moves the certified `homolog_db/` + report + provenance to the checkout on the success gate, clears the git-ignored `DONE` marker FIRST / writes it last, and the report lands only on the driver's all-gates-pass path (fail-closed). **NOTHING BUILT (§10.3):** no DB, no report, no scan, no cmsearch, no candidate count — this session authored machinery and **STOPPED at the §9.3 submit-ack** (the build + retrieval + `dvc add` are later sessions). **Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/mining/homolog_db.py`; `slurm/p2/build_homolog_db.sbatch`; `tests/unit/test_homolog_db.py`. No data artifact this session.

**Validation.** **In-env end-to-end proof on the cluster (the strongest check for pinned-version CLIs, [[verify-the-line-you-ship]]):** context7 carries no version-accurate BLAST/HMMER CLI content, so the *actual* driver was run through the *real* binaries in `tbox-homology` on a 3-genome toy — both probes self-recovered at their own `<acc>:c0` by **blastn** (pident 100.0, len 500, E 0.0) **and** **nhmmer** (E ≈ 1.8e-161); `blastdbcmd -info` cross-checked (3 seq / 3,600 bp == the concatenated totals); HMMER parsed **3.4**, BLAST **2.17.0**; a raw `blastn` dump confirmed `sseqid == GCA_T001.1:c0` — the `<accession>:c<ci>` subject-id scheme survives `makeblastdb`→`blastn` with **no** `-parse_seqids`. (A first toy used a period-4 sequence that BLAST's DUST filter masked entirely → an empty-hits failure that was the *fixture's* low complexity, not the driver's — regenerated with a PRNG.) **Unit tier** (no local pytest env, [[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]): a standalone runner in `tbox-finder-data` (py3.12) with a `pytest.raises` shim ran **29/29 PASS**. **Bite proven by source-sabotage (§8.7, `-B` to defeat stale pyc; restored by rewrite + diff since the module is new/untracked, [[sabotage-restore-untracked-file-git-checkout-noop]]):** disabling the integrity set-equality → the dropped-genome test flips RED; making the **blastn** leg accept any subject → the wrong-blast-genome test flips RED; making the **nhmmer** leg accept any target → the missing-nhmmer test flips RED; naming drift `:c`→`:C` → 3 tests flip. A first-pass self-recovery fixture with **both** legs wrong was inversion-blind (the nhmmer check masked the sabotaged blastn one, [[symmetric-count-fixture-blind-to-inversion]]) → split into per-engine-isolated tests, then each sabotage bites its own test. `black@25.11.0 --check` + `ruff@0.15.15` clean (line-length 100); the sbatch is `bash -n` clean and its only `rm` targets the untracked `DONE` marker + `/tmp` scratch (the [[sbatch-rm-of-tracked-path-fails-own-gate]] class). `sbatch --test-only` preflight is pending the §9.3 ack. **Decisions.** **No new ADR** — ADR-0006 A1 pins the target-DB identity + count and D7 the method; the build executes them, and the inclusion thresholds are P6-frozen (D17), so no design value was taken (§10.3). The `makehmmerdb` FM-index is built because `nhmmer` is the first-named D7 route and the FM-index is what makes it tractable over ~7 Gbp; the plain target FASTA (nhmmer fallback + cmsearch) + the BLAST DB together make all three D7 routes runnable — no threshold pinned. The DB indexes real fetched genomes; no fabricated count. No README line (phase-level; the Phase 2 headline lands at the phase-exit gate, §6.2). `dvc push` n/a this session (no artifact; `data/interim/homolog_db` is `dvc add`-ed in the result session). **Owed next:** the §9.3 `submit` ack → poll → artifact-based verify (`squeue` empty · `DONE` · report with `round_trip.all_recovered==true`) → LOCAL retrieval (`rsync` + `dvc add data/interim/homolog_db` + commit report/provenance) → then **only** the fetched-window→negative-pool path (ADR-0004 A4) remains before P2-10e can run a mining round. **Commit.** squash **`da27c77`** on `main` (PR [#82](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/82)); feature-branch commit on `p2-10cprime-homologdb`

## Step P2-10e-msa (certification + investigation) — 2026-07-26: the certification does NOT pass — the cmbuild-from-candidate de-novo route yields 0 covariation on real class-II data → decision: adopt LocARNA

**Inputs.** The machinery commit `6d20451` + the on-cluster homolog DB (15 GB) + 2,500 genomes + the committed class-II seed fixture. Prerequisite done: `tbox-infernal` (RNAfold 2.7.2 / INFERNAL 1.1.5) + `tbox-rscape` (R-scape 2.0.4.a, `backend_available()==True`) created on the cluster from the pinned locks. **Process.** §9.3 submit (user ack) → **job 748** (node `one`, ~110 s) ran clean and **fail-closed correctly**: the class-II seed recovered **0 blastn hits** at the control (megablast, E=1e-3, min_pident=60) → `sufficient=false` → exit 4 → no DONE, no certify report, **no false green**. On the user's "investigate before re-running", read-only cluster probes established: **(a)** the divergent homologs exist but need the sensitive **`-task blastn`** (megablast=0 even at E=10; classic blastn = 69 hits/62 genomes at E=10; nhmmer = 18 — *less* sensitive from a single seq); **(b)** they are short **conserved-core** matches (72–100 % identity but alignment length < 110 nt), so the shipped `min_cov=0.5` rejected all — the control was tuned for close full-length homologs, the opposite of the divergent-covariation goal; **(c)** a 10-seed sweep: raw distinct homologs are ample (median ~65) but the ≥20-after-permissive-filter count is seed-dependent (0–36); **(d) DECISIVE** — with the corrected sensitive search + permissive filter (E=10, min_pident=40, min_cov=0.2), seeds 6/42/48 each assemble ≥20 homologs (37/22/27 seqs, 2–3 consensus helices) yet R-scape reports **`total_covarying=0` → `failed` on EVERY seed**. **Outputs.** No code change, no artifact (investigation was read-only cluster probes; the temp `-task blastn` patch was applied only to the sacrificial cluster checkout and restored). **Validation.** n/a — this step's finding **is** that the validation gate (must-fire positive → covariation `passed`) **is not met**; `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` stays `False`, nothing flipped, nothing fabricated (§10.3). **Decisions.** Root cause (diagnosed, not a bug): the de-novo `#=GC SS_cons` is a **single candidate's RNAfold MFE fold** (cmbuild-from-one-sequence), not a *comparative consensus* — cmalign forces homologs into the wrong pairing, so R-scape tests the wrong columns and finds nothing. This is exactly why ADR-0006 **D7 names LocARNA** (Sankoff simultaneous fold+align → a genuine consensus) as its primary CM-free aligner; the "covariance model built from the candidates" alternative is the *weak* form when the CM comes from one MFE fold. **User decision (AskUserQuestion, 2026-07-26): adopt LocARNA.** ⇒ a follow-up **`P2-10e-msa-locarna` step, DESIGN first**: draft an **ADR-0002 env amendment** (a new `locarna`/`mlocarna` env pin + conda-lock — a §3.1/§7/§13 sign-off gate) + the methodology change (`align_candidate`: RNAfold→cmbuild→cmalign ⇒ mlocarna consensus), sign off, THEN ENCODE (amend env, re-implement `align_candidate`, re-run the certification — a fresh §9.3 submit-ack, also carrying the `-task blastn` fix + the permissive control cutoffs), THEN flip the flag + wire the mine_round legs. The seed-dependence of homolog recovery is **directionally safe** for production (a hard Tier-2N candidate → <20 homologs → `unavailable` → *spared*, never mined). **Commit.** squash **`73bd5be`** on `main` (PR [#85](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/85)); feature-branch dev-log addendum on `p2-10e-msa`

**Inputs.** The DESIGN sign-off (both amendments approved 2026-07-27; `P2-10e-msa-locarna-adr-draft.md`); the machinery commit `6d20451` (`mining/homolog_msa.py`, `slurm/p2/certify_homolog_msa.sbatch`); the job-748 root cause (a single candidate's RNAfold MFE fold ≠ a comparative consensus ⇒ R-scape `total_covarying=0` on class-II seeds 6/42/48, each ≥20 homologs); the mlocarna 2.0.1 CLI pinned from upstream source (context7 has NO LocARNA entry). **Process.** One atomic commit: **(1)** new 9th env `envs/locarna.yml` (`tbox-locarna`; `locarna` 2.0.1/`mlocarna` + `python` 3.12 + `biopython` 1.87; `viennarna` 2.7.2 pulled transitively) + `envs/locarna.conda-lock.yml` (conda-lock 4.0.2 `-p linux-64`, clean solve — no pip graph, so no A4/A8 hand-merge — `content_hash.linux-64 = c14a44e4…`, `locarna` build `pl5321h9948957_2`); **(2)** ADR-0002 **A13** + ADR-0006 **A3** (+ their `## Sign-off` lines); **(3)** `homolog_msa.py::align_candidate` rewritten around `mlocarna --stockholm --consensus-structure alifold --tgtdir <dir> --threads N` → `<dir>/results/result.stk` → R-scape direct (retired the RNAfold/cmbuild/cmalign helpers + the SS-alphabet consts; kept the `#=GC SS_cons` output guard; added `mlocarna_argv`, `assert_mlocarna_version`, an input-integrity guard, `PINNED_LOCARNA_VERSION="2.0.1"`), plus **`-task blastn`** in `blastn_argv`; **(4)** the sbatch Stage-2 env `tbox-infernal`→`tbox-locarna` + mlocarna version assert + control cutoffs `1e-3/60/0.5 → 10/40/0.2`; **(5)** `test_env_manifest.py` (8→9, `locarna`, spec↔lock) + `test_homolog_msa.py` (align tests → mlocarna path; version/input guards; code↔lock pin tie). **Outputs.** `envs/locarna.{yml,conda-lock.yml}`; the two ADR amendments; the rewritten producer + sbatch; the updated tests. No DVC artifact; no certification run; no flag flipped (§10.3). **Validation.** `PYTHONPATH=src pytest` (base 9.0.2): **40 passed** in `test_homolog_msa` + env-manifest; the mining-adjacent suite (covariation/mine_round/msa_shuffle/spare_rule/homolog_db/homolog_msa/env_manifest) = **187 passed, 0 failed**; a standalone runner proved **non-vacuity by sabotage** ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]], [[degenerate-fixture-generators]]): a look-alike `LocARNA 2.0.10` is rejected by the `\b` in the version guard, and an absent candidate + an SS_cons-less `result.stk` each raise. `ruff@0.15.15` (E,F,I,W,UP,B,SIM; line-length 100) + `black@25.11.0 --check` clean; `bash -n` on the sbatch clean; both amendments carry ≥2 §10.1 sources per claim (accessed 2026-07-27). The STEP's real gate (R-scape ≥1 covarying pair on ≥1 real class-II seed AND its matched column-shuffle `STATUS_FAILED`) is the SLURM certification re-run — a **fresh §9.3 submit-ack**, NOT covered by the DESIGN sign-off — the next action; a fail (mlocarna also 0-covariation on class-II) is a §7 stop. **Decisions.** context7 has no LocARNA → the mlocarna CLI (`--tgtdir`/`--stockholm`/`--consensus-structure alifold`/`--threads`; output `results/result.stk`; `--version` → `LocARNA 2.0.1`) was pinned from the v2.0.1 Perl driver + man page (a sourced research subagent, [[verify-the-line-you-ship]]). **Load-bearing correction:** mlocarna's default `--consensus-structure` is `none` (writes NO `#=GC SS_cons`), so `alifold` is required for R-scape to have a consensus; the output guard asserts the line is present. `--threads` kept small (LocARNA scaling caveat, `--cpu 2`). The homolog FASTA already carries the candidate as record 0 (`search_homologs`), so it IS the single mlocarna input; `candidate_fasta` is retained for the unchanged public signature + an input-integrity guard. A SEPARATE 9th env (not folded into `envs/infernal.yml`) keeps the GATE-1-load-bearing infernal lock byte-frozen (the A11/A12 precedent). No new ADR sign-off owed — A13/A3 pre-signed 2026-07-27; the ML stack (D8) untouched. **Commit.** squash **`73bd5be`** on `main` (PR [#85](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/85)); feature-branch encode commit on `p2-10e-msa`; certification re-run + `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE→True` + `mine_round.sbatch` legs (a)–(d) deferred to the fresh §9.3 submit-ack.

## Step P2-10e-msa-locarna (certification + RESULT) — 2026-07-27: the CM-free MSA supply is covariation-CERTIFIED (nhmmer + mlocarna; R-scape positive PASSED / matched-shuffle FAILED) — flag-flip + leg-wiring deferred (a producer gap)

**Inputs.** The ENCODE commit `122a424` (mlocarna `align_candidate` + `envs/locarna.yml`); the A1 target DB `data/interim/homolog_db/` (job 741) + 2,500 `data/interim/production_genomes/*.fna` (job 739) + the real class-II seed `tests/fixtures/rscape/classII_sub.sto` (row 0, 221 nt), all staged on the cluster; `envs/{locarna,rscape}.conda-lock.yml`. **Process.** Three fresh §9.3 submit-acks (the DESIGN sign-off covers no submit). **Job 755** (blastn 10/40/0.2): only **4 homologs** — a login-node diagnostic showed `-task blastn` finds 69 hits but ALL short (~20-33 nt) high-identity anchors on a conserved core (pident irrelevant — every hit ≥89%; only coverage cuts them), so blastn cannot extend across a structured RNA's divergent flanks. User (AskUserQuestion) approved switching the engine blastn→**nhmmer** at E≤100/cov≥0.5 (within ADR-0006 D7 — nhmmer is a sanctioned menu engine, inclusion thresholds "frozen at P6", no number to contradict; commit `d2b57ab`); the FM-index recovers FULL-LENGTH divergent homologs (24 targets, ≥50% query coverage). **Job 760** (nhmmer): search 23 homologs, mlocarna aligned, but certify CRASHED — `ValueError: zip() argument 49 is shorter than arguments 1-48` in `msa_shuffle.shuffle_alignment_columns`: mlocarna's `result.stk` is INTERLEAVED Stockholm (24 rows × 3 blocks, widths 120/120/49 = 289) but `read_pfam_alignment` assumed one-line-per-sequence Pfam — it appended 72 ragged rows and overwrote `#=GC SS_cons` to the last block's fragment. Fixed the reader to accumulate sequence + `#=GC` fragments by name/tag and join across blocks (identity on unwrapped input ⇒ the P2-10b fixture byte-locks are unchanged) + a real-fixture regression `tests/fixtures/rscape/mlocarna_interleaved.sto` (the job-760 output) + the align docstring correction (commit `f19e548`). **Job 766** (fixed): **GREEN**. **Outputs.** `data/processed/audits/homolog_msa_certify_report.json` (`certified=true`, `positive=passed`, `shuffled=failed`, depth 24, composition/depth/width/SS_cons all matched) + `reports/p2/homolog_msa_search_report.json` + `data/interim/homolog_msa/certified_positive.sto` (git-committed directly — 10 KB, `dvc` absent locally, byte-identical to the committed fixture) + `data/interim/homolog_msa/provenance.json`. `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` stays **False**; `mine_round.sbatch` legs (a)-(d) stay stubbed. **Validation.** SLURM job 766 (node `one`, CPU-only, ~2 min); §9.3 artifact-based verify all green (squeue empty · DONE marker · `.err` 0 bytes · `certified==true`); `verification: artifact-based (sacct off)`. Parser fix: 13/13 standalone (both fixture-locks byte-identical + the interleaved regression) + source-sabotage bites (the old parser gives 72 rows and the exact production `ValueError`); ruff@0.15.15 + black@25.11.0 clean. **Decisions.** The GREEN certification proves the ADR-0006 A2 covariation-(a) producibility claim for a real divergent class-II locus. **§7 scope discovery (AskUserQuestion → "land cert now; producer = a new step"):** the TODO's RESULT plan — flip `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE→True` + wire the legs — cannot be done coherently, because the certified producer is NOT composed into the mining loop: `window_candidates_to_mining` attaches the default all-UNAVAILABLE `SpareRuleEvidence` and nothing runs per-candidate search→align→covariation to populate it (`covariation_spare_status` is invoked only by the standalone `certify` CLI). Flipping the flag would pass readiness while every FP carries UNAVAILABLE covariation evidence ⇒ the spare rule spares them all ⇒ a report of zeroes that reads as "nothing to mine" and a lying readiness gate ([[matched-control-before-certifying]], [[control-matchedness-must-be-asserted]]). The NEXT STEP is a per-candidate covariation-evidence PRODUCER (candidate → `search_homologs` nhmmer → `align_candidate` mlocarna → `covariation_spare_status` → `SpareRuleEvidence.covariation`) wired into `scan_substrate_windows`, which raises a real mining-time compute-budget question (mlocarna ~2-3 min/candidate, no threading past ~2-3, × hundreds-thousands of FPs/round — plausibly its own ADR). **Commit.** squash **`73bd5be`** on `main` (PR [#85](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/85)); the RESULT commit on branch `p2-10e-msa` (preceded by `d2b57ab` nhmmer-engine + `f19e548` interleaved-parse fix); the flag-flip + producer + N=4 RUN deferred.

`write_fp_manifest`/`read_fp_manifest` (leg b→c/d handoff, covariation-producer-manifest-shaped so the producer reads it directly); `scan_admissible_genomes`/`load_admissible_accessions` (leg a) + `apply_spare_rule` (leg d) + the `scan-shard`/`collect`/`admissible-accessions`/`apply-spare-rule` CLIs. **(4)** `slurm/p2/mine_round.sbatch` legs a–d (replace the ready-path `exit 2`): (a) 8-way GPU-sharded scan → (b) collect+shard → submit (c) the decoupled CPU producer array `mine_round_producer.sbatch` + (d) the DDP retrain `mine_round_retrain.sbatch` (afterok), then exit (releasing the GPUs during the CPU producer, A10 Pin 2). **(5)** `slurm/p2/mine_round_measure.sbatch` — the A10 Phase-1 measurement (a single 8-GPU-node job: 8-way scan → real N₀ + a deterministic K≥50 accession-sorted producer sample → per-stage wall + depth → measure report). **Outputs.** ADR-0005 A10; `mining/covariation_producer.py`; `mine_round.py` + `homolog_msa.py` additions; the 4 sbatch files; `tests/unit/test_covariation_producer.py` + `test_mine_round.py`/`test_homolog_msa.py` additions. No DVC artifact, **no flag flip** (`MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` stays `False` until the A10 Phase-2 pin), no SLURM submit (§10.3). **Validation.** No local pytest env ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]) → a standalone runner in `tbox-finder-data` (numpy/pandas) ran **27 checks, 0 failed** across the load-bearing pure logic (spec/manifest/slug/sample/partition; merge + disjoint guard + `load_status_map` rows↔status agreement; `search_shard` fail-closed on an out-of-contig candidate AND fail-**loud** `HomologDbError` on a missing binary; `score_shard(None)`→`unavailable`; `measure_report` N₀+median+envelope; `resolve_candidate_sequence` half-open + OOB; the `window_candidates_to_mining` status stamp + fail-closed absent-id; the FP-manifest round-trip + producer-reader compat + retrain-leg status stamp; `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE is False`). **Bite proven by source-sabotage (§8.7, `python -B` per [[sabotage-restores-masked-by-pycache]]):** the fail-closed default `unavailable → "failed"` flips the two absent-id checks RED; disabling **both** dedup guards lets a duplicate `candidate_id` slip the merge; the `resolve` half-open `[start:end] → [start-1:end]` breaks the coordinate checks — each restored green (PASS=27). `ruff@0.15.15` (E,F,I,W,UP,B,SIM; line-length 100) + `black@25.11.0 --check` clean; `bash -n` on all 4 sbatch clean; all 6 py files `py_compile`; snakemake DAG untouched (no rule added). **Decisions.** **No new ADR sign-off** — A10 is pre-signed (2026-07-27); §10.1 N/A (compute-orchestration/budget-governance). The producer is a **bash orchestrator, not one function** — the certified chain spans 3 mutually-incompatible conda envs (`tbox-homology`/`tbox-locarna`/`tbox-rscape`) and a single Python process cannot switch envs, so there is no in-process `candidate → status` entry and cannot be one (each stage is a shard-level CLI subcommand). **⚠ §7 finding surfaced for the user (weigh BEFORE the Phase-2 RUN / flag-flip, not resolved here):** with the producer populating `any_helix_rscape`, the spare rule STILL spares **every** candidate at P2 — `is_mining_excluded` fail-closes on **any** `unavailable` disjunct, and `relaxed_architecture` + `downstream_aaRS_synteny` are structurally unavailable (no backend), so mining yield is **structurally 0** regardless of covariation status (verified empirically: cov=failed and cov=passed both → spared; only all-three-`failed` mines). The producer scoring changes *which* candidates are `unavailable` vs `failed`/`passed`, not the *mined* set — so the N=4 RUN would retrain on 0 new hard negatives. This is pre-existing signed spare-rule semantics (ADR-0006 D9 row 5 / D11 / A2 fail-closed sparing; ADR-0005 D14), NOT introduced here, so it does not block this signed ENCODE (whose deliverable is the producer machinery + the A10 measurement of N₀ + per-candidate wall, both well-defined). It IS handled honestly downstream: `mine_round_retrain.sbatch` skips the retrain on `n_mined=0` with an explicit no-op message rather than emitting a checkpoint trained on nothing new ([[matched-control-before-certifying]]). ## Step P2-10e-msa-producer (A10 Phase-1 PROBE — RESULT) — 2026-07-28: measured 23.87 win/s/GPU (~2.8× below the A9 estimate) — the job-793 TIMEOUT was throughput-bound, not a stall; FPs/window = 0 over 30k windows

At 23.87 win/s/GPU the heaviest a2 shard (524,959 windows) needs 524,959 / 23.87 ≈ **6.1 h** — just over the old 6 h wall, exactly the TIMEOUT. **Decisions.** No ADR (A10 Pin 1 measure-first; this is the measurement, not a pin). The full Phase-1 measurement (`mine_round_measure.sbatch`) must (a) set `--time` well past 6 h (gpu partition TIMELIMIT is infinite) — ~8 h clears the heaviest shard — and/or (b) close the ~2.8× throughput gap with a code fix (scan-shard batching / fp16 / dataloader), which would bring the heaviest shard to ~2.2 h; plus the persistent per-shard progress this probe demonstrated. ## Step P2-10e-msa-producer (A10 Phase-1 FULL MEASUREMENT — size + harden) — 2026-07-28: `--time` 6 h→12 h + persistent per-shard throughput progress in the 8 GPU legs; the ~2.8× batch=1 scan fix DEFERRED to its own validated step (the honest-N₀ measurement runs the probe-validated scan)

**Inputs.** The job-806 probe RESULT (`reports/p2/mine_round_probe.json`: **23.87 win/s/GPU** robust across genomes, 0 FP / 30k windows at τ=0.9); `slurm/p2/mine_round_measure.sbatch` (`81612f9`→`0910415`, whose fixed 6 h wall TIMED OUT as job 793); the scan-shard throughput instrumentation already shipped by the probe ENCODE (`1c5850a`: `--progress-out`/`--flush-every-windows`/`--max-windows` + the SIGTERM→SystemExit finally-flush, unit-tested). **Process.** A LOCAL sizing + hardening session, ONE atomic commit touching only the sbatch (the Python instrumentation is already in place). **(1) WALL.** `--time` 6 h→**12 h**: at the measured 23.87 win/s/GPU the heaviest a2 shard (524,959 windows under `split -n l/8`) needs 524,959/23.87 ≈ **6.1 h** of scan (exactly the old-6 h TIMEOUT) + the ~2 h CPU producer phase → ~8.1 h; 12 h clears it with margin (the gpu partition TIMELIMIT is *infinite*, so a longer soft ceiling is free). **(2) PER-SHARD PROGRESS.** threaded `--progress-out reports/p2/mine_round_measure_shard<i>.json --flush-every-windows 500` into each of the 8 backgrounded `scan-shard` legs — persistent (reports/, NOT the `/tmp` `$JOB_SCRATCH` the EXIT trap wipes), flushed every 500 windows + on the wall-clock SIGTERM (the `--progress-out` path auto-installs the preserve-partials handler), so a second timeout still pins each shard's last win/s/GPU + FP-rate + `in_progress_accession` — the exact diagnostic job 793 lacked (its EXIT trap auto-cleaned the evidence). **(3)** header sizing/hardening rationale + a VERIFY-on-timeout note (read the per-shard files to tell a slow scan from a stalled genome). **Outputs.** `slurm/p2/mine_round_measure.sbatch` only (+ this stanza). **No Python change, no new unit test** (the threaded instrumentation is the probe's, unit-tested at `1c5850a`); no DVC artifact; no flag flip (`MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` stays `False`); no submit (§10.3). **Validation.** `bash -n` clean; no `rm`/deletion added (only the pre-existing `rm -f "$DONE"` on the untracked marker + the `/tmp` EXIT trap → `test_sbatch_rm_targets` unaffected); no test shape-locks the measure sbatch (only a `test_covariation_producer` docstring mentions it); `--progress-out`/`--flush-every-windows` are the exact shipped `scan-shard` argparse tokens (the probe sbatch uses the same, CI-green). The step's real gate is the §9.3 preflight `sbatch --test-only` at the submit-ack. **Decisions.** **No ADR** (A10 Pin 1 measure-first, unchanged; the sizing pins no budget/threshold); §10.1 N/A (operational hardening, no bio/stat claim). **⚠ The ~2.8× throughput gap is DIAGNOSED but the fix is DEFERRED, deliberately.** Root cause (traced through the code, not guessed): the mining scan forwards **one 1024-nt window per model call** — `_scan_one_window` → `scan.scan_sequence` on a ≤1024-nt substrate window → `tile_windows` emits exactly one window → `scan_encoded_windows` runs a **batch of 1**, so `DEFAULT_SCAN_BATCH=8` never engages and the A4000 is starved (the A9 67.68 win/s/GPU estimate assumed the batched throughput). Batching *across* substrate windows is result-preserving in principle (each window is an independent forward; the scanner already documents batch size as "changes speed and peak VRAM, never the result"), but it is a numerics-sensitive change to the scan hot path (also consumed by GATE-4 P2-14) whose batched-vs-unbatched forward equivalence **has no validation path this session** — CI installs no torch (torch tiers are env-var-gated OFF), no local env carries torch+pytest ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]], [[no-env-has-torch-and-sklearn]]), and WSL2 CUDA is unreliable for RNA inference ([[wsl2-cuda-unknown-error-large-rna]]). Bundling an only-cluster-verifiable scan change into the run that produces the headline N₀ risks silently corrupting it (§10.3), whereas this measurement runs the exact scan the probe (job 806) already validated and the 12 h wall accommodates it at 23.87 win/s. So the batching fix is carved out as its own step (implement `scan_many_sequences`-style cross-window batching in `infer/scan.py` reusing the shared forward + `reconcile_windows` per window; lock result-preservation with a batched-vs-unbatched equivalence unit; then re-measure) — the better home for the ~2.8×→~1× win, ahead of the N=4 RUN where 4 rounds of scan actually pay for it. The full Phase-1 measurement is a **fresh §9.3 submit-ack** (its own — the sizing does not authorize a submit). **Commit.** squash **`9d06992`** on `main` (PR [#86](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/86)); feature-branch commit on branch `p2-10e-msa-producer` (the measurement submit + the A10 Phase-2 pin deferred to the fresh §9.3 submit-ack).

## Step P2-10e-msa-producer (RESULT PR — CI fix) — 2026-07-28: make `mine_round_producer.sbatch`'s stale-marker `rm` statically resolvable so the tracked-path gate passes; land the branch on `main`

**Inputs.** Branch `p2-10e-msa-producer` @ `8e5f899` (7 commits ahead of `main`), whose CI has been **red since the ENCODE `81612f9`** on one test: `test_no_sbatch_deletes_a_git_tracked_path[mine_round_producer.sbatch]` (`tests/unit/test_sbatch_rm_targets.py`; the [[sbatch-rm-of-tracked-path-fails-own-gate]] gate). The red went unseen because no local env runs pytest ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]); the earlier stanzas' `bash -n` clean is syntax-only and this gate is a static analysis of `rm` targets, not syntax. **Process.** The gate resolves each `rm` argument and fails **closed** on anything it cannot resolve. `mine_round_producer.sbatch` built its per-shard paths with `OK_MARKER="$(printf "%s/shard_%03d.SHARD_OK" "$STATUS_DIR" "$TASK")"` — a **command substitution**, which the parser deliberately never guesses at (`test_a_command_substitution_is_never_guessed_at`), so `rm -f "$OK_MARKER"` resolved to the widest `*` and matched **all 548 tracked paths** (e.g. `.coderabbit.yaml`). The marker itself is harmless — an *untracked* runtime `.SHARD_OK` under `$ROUND_DIR/status/` (= `data/processed/mining/round_<k>/status/`, itself a `data/` staging path) — so this is a false positive from an unresolvable expression, not a real tracked-path deletion. Fix: build the paths with plain interpolation, zero-padding via `printf -v TASK3 "%03d" "$TASK"` (preserving make-shards' `shard_{i:03d}.json` naming, `covariation_producer.py:199`) exactly like the sibling `mine_round_retrain.sbatch:39-40` clears its own `.DONE`. Byte-identical runtime behavior; the `rm` now resolves to `*/status/shard_*.SHARD_OK` — a suffix matching **no** tracked path. **Outputs.** `slurm/p2/mine_round_producer.sbatch` only (+ this stanza). No Python/test change (the test is correct — not weakened); no DVC artifact; no flag flip (`MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` stays `False`); no submit; nothing runs. **Validation.** `bash -n` clean on all 5 p2 mine_round sbatch; a standalone reproduction of the CI test's own `_rm_targets`/`_offence`/`_tracked_paths` (imported from the shipped test module) reports **0 offenders** for the fixed producer and confirms the `rm` is still *detected* (resolves to `*/status/shard_*.SHARD_OK`, not silently dropped); a full sweep of every non-`_KNOWN_DEFECTIVE` sbatch reports 0 offenders (no regression); a **sabotage bite** reverting to the `$(printf …)` form re-flags all 548 tracked paths (the gate still bites), then restores byte-identical. **Decisions.** No ADR (an operational sbatch static-analyzability fix; A9/A10/A2 untouched — the run's semantics, budget, thresholds, and the deferred RUN are all unchanged); §10.1 N/A (no bio/stat claim). This unblocks the RESULT PR (§5.1): PR base `main` ← head `p2-10e-msa-producer` → CodeRabbit → green CI → squash-merge → FF local `main`. **Commit.** squash **`9d06992`** on `main` (PR [#86](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/86)); feature-branch commit on branch `p2-10e-msa-producer`.

## Step P2-11 (ENCODE) — 2026-07-28: wire a `label_source=naive` selector through the trainer→datamodule + the class-II-CM-naive ablation sbatch; the RUN is a fresh §9.3 submit-ack

**Inputs.** `slurm/p2/train_production.sbatch` (the P2-10d′-b twin, job 680) as the clone base; `src/tbox_finder/{train/train_stage1.py,data/window_dataset.py}`; `src/tbox_finder/labels.py:244-245` (the P0-20 naive derivation, already emitting the `naive_label_string` column into `labels_v0.parquet`); `conf/train/stage1.yaml`; the 5 staged parquets (context_v0, labels_v0, split_assignments [LFS], mining_pool_v0, decoys_v0 — the P2-10d′-b SEED curriculum, mining parked). Governing: PRD §5 mech 3 / §8 / §10.1 / §2.3; **ADR-0004 D1/D5** (the label-source flag, signed 2026-07-10 — "the two checkpoints share one leakage-controlled partition, differing only in label source"); **ADR-0005 D9** (anti-mimicry Stage-1-only). **Process.** A read-only 5-agent scout established the load-bearing finding: **P0 built the naive DERIVATION but not the trainer wiring** — `window_dataset` hard-coded the production `label_string` column and `_cfg_from_mapping` silently drops unknown Hydra keys, so a bare `label_source=naive` would have been ignored and the "naive" run would have trained on the CM-bearing labels it exists to withhold, its own gate passing (CLAUDE.md §10.3; the anti-mimicry test would then measure RF00230 mimicry, the exact confound PRD §5 mech 3 rules out). Building the selector IS P2-11's own Rule/Entry ("train_stage1.py label-source=naive"), an already-signed mechanism (ADR-0004 D1/D5 name P2-11) — no new ADR, no §7 deviation. **(1) SELECTOR.** `window_dataset.resolve_label_column(label_source)` maps `production→label_string` / `naive→naive_label_string` and FAILS LOUD on anything else (never a silent fallback to production); `NAIVE_LABEL_STRING_COL`/`LABEL_SOURCE_COLUMNS` added. **(2) MERGE.** `_merge_corpus_tables(label_column=…)` selects the chosen column, guards a stale production-only labels table (raises if `naive_label_string` absent), and normalises it to `LABEL_STRING_COL` so `_corpus_record` reads one column name; `load_corpus_records(label_source=…)` threads it and RECORDS the resolved `label_source`/`label_column` in its report. **(3) TRAINER.** `Stage1TrainConfig.label_source: str = "production"` (a real field → `_cfg_from_mapping` threads it, cannot be silently dropped) + `__post_init__` rejects any non-{production,naive} value at construction; `cfg.label_source` threaded into the data build; the resolved source surfaced in the run report's `class_counts_scope` (and free in `diagnostics.config` via `asdict`). **(4) CONFIG.** `conf/train/stage1.yaml` gains `label_source: production` (the job-669 struct-mode lesson: a CLI-overridable field MUST exist as a yaml key). **(5) SBATCH.** `slurm/p2/train_classII_naive.sbatch` — a byte-for-byte clone of the production trainer with exactly one changed override (`label_source=naive`), re-pointed outputs (job-name/report/DONE/ckpt `stage1_classII_naive`/lock/provenance), the `BUILD`→`JOB_SCRATCH` post-job-789 rename ([[conda-toolchain-clobbers-build-host]]), and a **runtime label-source guard**: after the run, before publishing the checkpoint, it re-derives the source from the report (`diagnostics.config.label_source` AND `class_counts_scope.label_source`/`.label_column`) and REFUSES to move the checkpoint unless all say naive — so a mis-wired naive run produces NO DONE. **Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/data/window_dataset.py` (+selector/merge/loader), `src/tbox_finder/train/train_stage1.py` (+field/validation/threading/report), `conf/train/stage1.yaml` (+key), `slurm/p2/train_classII_naive.sbatch` (new), `tests/unit/test_label_source_wiring.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_sbatch_overrides.py` (+`label_source` both-halves + naive-token contract) (+ this stanza). No checkpoint yet (the RUN is the submit-ack); `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` untouched (unrelated). **Validation.** No local pytest env → the wiring tiers run in a standalone `tbox-finder-data` runner (import confirmed torch-free: `window_dataset` imports torch lazily) — the selector map/raise, the `_merge_corpus_tables` naive-column identity (a class-II-like `r1` where prod≠naive, so a copy-of-production selector fails on IDENTITY not count, [[symmetric-count-fixture-blind-to-inversion]]), the missing-column fail-closed, and the `load_corpus_records` thread+report keys — all green, with source-sabotage bites (selector collapse → RED; merge ignores `label_column` → RED). `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean; `bash -n` clean on the new sbatch; the rm-target gate sweep clean (the sbatch's only `rm` is the named-path stale-output clear, `$REPORT` excluded). The Hydra struct-mode composition of the sbatch's own tokens is validated at the §9.3 preflight in `tbox-ml-dna` (and by `test_sbatch_overrides.py` in CI). **Decisions.** No new ADR (ADR-0004 D1/D5 + ADR-0005 D9 already sign and name the naive run; this ENCODE builds the signed, anticipated mechanism); §10.1 N/A (engineering wiring, no bio/stat claim). Compute is MEASURED from the P2-10d′-b twin (job 680: ~2.35 h train wall / ~18.8 GPU-h, `gpu:a4000:8`, cpus 16, mem 64G, seed 42), NOT the stale imp.md `cpus:64/mem:200GB` estimate — the ablation mirrors the real production sbatch. The RUN is a fresh §9.3 submit-ack (Stops: SLURM submit-ack); the checkpoint's `dvc add` + provenance + the PR land at the RESULT commit. **Commit.** squash **`fe6e43b`** on `main` (PR [#87](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/87)); feature-branch commit on branch `p2-11-classII-naive`.

The checkpoint identity moved out of two module constants into a torch-free **closed allow-list** (`models/backbone_registry.py`), from which `caduceus_backbone` now *derives* `REPO_ID`/`REVISION`/`EXPECTED_PARAM_COUNT`/`D_MODEL`/`N_LAYER` rather than restating them; `load_caduceus_ps` gained a `checkpoint:` selector, and it now gates the **measured** parameter count and the loaded `config.d_model` against the entry as well as the revision. `Stage1TrainConfig` gained a `backbone` field with `__post_init__` rejection (and the same for the ADR-0005 D15 order-destroying `rc_combine`), `conf/train/stage1.yaml` gained the matching struct-mode key with exactly one home, `build_model` sizes the seg head from the **measured** `d_model` (the ~471k checkpoint is 118, not 256), the report's `backbone` block became the resolved + measured identity at `schema_version` `"3"`, and `diagnostics.swept_by` gained `backbone: "P2-12"`. New: `slurm/p2/ablate_stage1.sbatch` (`--array=0-3`), the separate 1-GPU `slurm/p2/backbone_throughput.sbatch` + `eval/backbone_throughput.py`, and `train/ablation_table.py`. **Outputs.** ADR-0003 A3 + ADR-0002 A14 · `src/tbox_finder/models/backbone_registry.py` · `src/tbox_finder/eval/backbone_throughput.py` · `src/tbox_finder/train/ablation_table.py` · the two sbatch files · edits to `models/caduceus_backbone.py`, `models/rc_combine.py`, `models/stage1_segmenter.py`, `train/train_stage1.py`, `conf/train/stage1.yaml`, `.gitignore` · `tests/unit/test_backbone_registry.py`, `tests/unit/test_ablation_table.py`, two new tests in `tests/unit/test_sbatch_overrides.py` · this stanza. No GPU ran; no measured artifact was produced.

**Validation.** All green, and all of it executed rather than read. (a) The **three checkpoint identities were verified against the Hugging Face API** on 2026-07-29 — revisions, and identical `trust_remote_code` modeling-file manifests, which is what makes A14 an add with no lockfile change — and all three were **loaded on CPU** in `tbox-ml-dna`: **7,725,312 / 1,934,592 / 470,702** parameters. The production figure reproduces the independently code-pinned `EXPECTED_PARAM_COUNT` to the integer, which is what licenses recording the other two as expectations a run must match. (b) ADR-0003 A3's arithmetic was **re-derived from the 36 committed sweep reports**, not transcribed: 1,160 steps × world_size 8 uniform across all 36; GPU-h min 1.5063 / mean 1.5509 / max 1.6201; promoted point 1.6095 GPU-h / 0.2012 wall-h; worst wall 0.2025 h; baseline CI [0.9125, 0.9550] at point 0.9386 with `rc_combine=concat`, `use_crf=false`. (c) The sbatch's **own tokens, extracted from the shipped bytes** ([[verify-the-line-you-ship]]), compose in `tbox-ml-dna` for all four legs against both `train/stage1` (what the CI gate uses, from the `hydra.main` decorator) and `train/stage1_best` (what the job actually passes), and reach the dataclass with the promoted axes intact — the [[hydra-struct-mode-override-needs-yaml-key]] pre-ack. (d) `bash -n` on both sbatch files, and the **shipped** `tests/unit/test_sbatch_rm_targets.py` helpers imported standalone: the two new files' only `rm` targets resolve to `reports/p2/ablation/status/leg_*.OK` and `reports/p2/status/backbone_throughput.OK`, matching **no** tracked path — both jobs write their reports to node-local `JOB_SCRATCH` and copy back afterwards, so neither can repeat the P2-10d′-c defect that disabled `sweep_stage1.sbatch`. (e) **45 new unit tests pass** under a standalone runner ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]) and **17 source-sabotage bites are all credited by name** — each breaks one fail-closed clause and turns RED the specific test meant to catch it, with the file restored by rewriting the original bytes and re-verifying its sha256 ([[sabotage-attribution-names-the-test]], [[sabotage-restore-untracked-file-git-checkout-noop]], `python -B` throughout). (f) A **regression diff against unmodified `main`** over ten affected unit modules returns an **identical failure set** (all pre-existing xfail-strict / real-pytest-fixture cases), plus two new passes; `test_sbatch_overrides` is 18/18 in `tbox-ml-dna`. (g) `ruff check` clean, `black 25.11.0 --check` clean.

**Decisions.** Three worth recording. (1) The ablation reducer is a **separate module**, not a widening of `select_best.SWEPT_AXES` — widening it in place would have silently changed the committed `reports/p2/sweep_selection.json` and the shape-lock test over it — and it *reuses* `point_problems` / `load_reports` / `cross_point_consistency` rather than forking them. It **ranks on the lower CI bound, names no winner**, and reports `separated_from_baseline` as a **three-valued** verdict so "could not be measured" cannot render as "separated"; with four legs on an 830-record fold the expected and reportable answer is that no axis separates. (2) The throughput probe is a **separate 1-GPU job**, not a fifth array task: scanning is inference, and reserving an 8-GPU node for a ten-minute measurement would waste the reservation and add noise to a sharing leg's timings. Its report carries its own scope disclosure — seeded synthetic windows measure a *shape's* forward cost, which is an argument from Mamba's fixed-shape dense ops, not a genome-scan rate. (3) The averaged-RC arm is **absent by decision, not by omission**: PRD:133/:212 + ADR-0005 D15 forbid it outright, `FORBIDDEN_RC_COMBINE` raises, and a unit test asserts it never appears in the shipped leg table — the document-precedence conflict resolved at DESIGN, now enforced in code. Two provenance misattributions were also corrected in passing (`models/rc_combine.py` and `models/stage1_segmenter.py` credited ADR-0002 for a constraint ADR-0005 D15 owns). §10.1 N/A: no biological claim is asserted here; the external checkpoint identities were verified directly against the HF API and by loading the weights. **Commit.** squash **`912508f`** on `main` (PR [#88](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/88)); feature-branch commit on branch `p2-12-ablations`.

(c) The `.err` files were **SCANNED, not zero-gated** — the four array tasks are each exactly 3,249 B of W&B offline chatter with **0** hits on `Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|OOM|Killed|CUDA error|FATAL`; job 884's is 0 B. (e) Independently of that guard, each retrieved report re-reads as `full_fold: true` on the 830-record / 469-block `selection_val` fold with **zero measured leakage** against `inner_train` (0 shared record ids, 0 shared cluster ids), `n_boot` 2000, seed 42, `env_lock` identical across all five rows. (f) The reducer's own validator **re-derives** each `separated_from_baseline` verdict from the recorded intervals rather than trusting the stored boolean and agreed on all five rows (exit 0); `cross_point_consistency.all_agree` is **false** for exactly one field — `git_sha`, because the reused baseline was trained at `4c723fd` — which is the disclosed-not-gated difference the module documents, and every other field agrees. (g) `provenance.git_dirty` is true on all four legs with `git_dirty_paths == ['data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet']`, i.e. the rsync-staged corpus inside `_DATA_STAGING_PREFIXES`, which is why `provenance_complete` still passes.

**Cost, re-derived rather than assumed.** Per-leg node-reserved (wall × 8): `rc_gate` 2.064, `head_crf` 6.091, `size_d256_l4` 0.722, `size_d118_l4` 0.711 → **9.589 GPU-h** for the array, plus ≈0.1 GPU-h for the 1-GPU probe ⇒ **≈9.69 GPU-h against ADR-0003 A3's pre-registered ≤ 18 GPU-h bound**, and within a rounding of A3's ≈9.5 point estimate. A3's per-leg *training* basis (Σ`step_seconds` × world_size ⁄ 3600) measures **8.1862 GPU-h** over the four legs against the 6.48 the 1.6201 basis predicted. **Disclosure (§10.3): the aggregate held, but not uniformly.** The CRF leg alone consumed 6.091 GPU-h node-reserved against a 1.889 basis — **3.2×**, far beyond the single **+0.94 GPU-h (+25%)** allowance A3 carried for the two legs whose per-step cost was unmeasured — while the two small-checkpoint legs came in at ~38% of theirs. A3 predicted exactly that second effect ("bounded **at** the 7.73M rate although both are strictly fewer FLOPs"), so the enumeration absorbed the CRF overrun for the reason it was built conservative, not by luck. Any future budget carrying a CRF leg should price it at ≈3× a linear-head leg, not +25%. Relatedly, `--time=02:00:00` gave the CRF leg **2.6×** headroom over its measured 0.761 wall-h, not the "~10×" the header claimed off the 0.2025 h sweep basis; the header is corrected in this commit.

**Result.** Ranked on the lower CI bound (the conservative statistic; the reducer names no winner, and PRD §10.1's shipped-config decision is P2-14's):

| leg | axis | min-core-F1 | 95% CI | Δ vs baseline | separated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `head_crf` | head: +CRF | 0.9416 | [0.9196, 0.9571] | +0.0029 | no |
| **baseline** (reused P2-06) | concat / linear / 7.73M | 0.9386 | [0.9125, 0.9550] | — | — |
| `rc_gate` | RC: `gate` | 0.9242 | [0.9005, 0.9387] | −0.0145 | no |
| `size_d256_l4` | 1.93M, seqlen-1k | 0.9191 | [0.8920, 0.9412] | −0.0196 | no |
| `size_d118_l4` | 471k, seqlen-1k | 0.8890 | [0.8581, 0.9047] | −0.0497 | **yes** |

Forward-only scan throughput at the held 1024/512 geometry, one A4000, fp32, batch 8: **69.49** win/s/GPU (7.73M, peak 0.334 GiB) · **268.41** (1.93M, **3.86×**, 0.237 GiB) · **423.54** (471k, **6.10×**, 0.282 GiB).

**Decisions.** (1) **One axis separates, and the honest reading is a negative result about the smallest checkpoint.** `size_d118_l4`'s interval [0.8581, 0.9047] lies entirely below the baseline's lower bound 0.9125, so the 471k checkpoint is measurably *worse*; the downward search has found its floor. (2) **The four non-separating rows must not be read as equivalence.** Non-overlap is a conservative separation test — overlap means "not distinguishable at this power on 830 records / 469 blocks", not "the same". This is why the reducer's verdict is three-valued and why no winner is named here. (3) **The size axis now has both halves, and they point in opposite directions**: the 1.93M checkpoint buys **3.86×** scan throughput while its accuracy interval still overlaps the baseline's, whereas the 471k checkpoint buys 6.10× and separates downward. That is the shape PRD §10.1's *throughput-driven* downward search was specified to produce, and it is the input P2-14 needs — but the arm is a **joint size × pretraining-context** change (both small checkpoints are seqlen-1k against production's seqlen-131k), so no delta may be attributed to parameter count alone. (4) **An unplanned corroboration of the deferred P2-10e scan-batch diagnosis.** That diagnosis predicted a ~2.8× throughput loss from forwarding the mining scan at batch 1; this probe measures the production checkpoint at **69.49** win/s/GPU batched against the mining probe's measured **23.87** at batch 1 on the same hardware and geometry — a ratio of **2.91×**. The comparison is not exact (the mining path also carries candidate-calling and reconciliation), so it corroborates rather than closes; the fix remains its own deferred step. The batched figure also lands close to ADR-0005 A9's 67.68 win/s/GPU estimate, which the batch-1 measurement had appeared to contradict. §10.1 N/A: nothing here asserts a biological fact — these are compute measurements and a selection-rung model comparison. **This table is not a generalization result** (`is_science: false`, `gate4_graded: false`); GATE-4 is graded at P2-14 on the real leave-one-order-out holdout. **Commit.** squash **`912508f`** on `main` (PR [#88](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/88)); feature-branch commit on branch `p2-12-ablations`.

## Step P2-12 (RESULT — review round) — 2026-07-29: CodeRabbit found the RC directionality invariant was unfalsifiable; make it measured, and the `rc_gate` leg's compliance becomes a re-run

**Inputs.** PR [#88](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/88) at `9b3a09b`; a **real** CodeRabbit CLI review (6 findings over 26 files) after the GitHub check returned only `Review rate limited` — the Fair-Usage notice, which is a **green check that is not a review** ([[coderabbit-fair-usage-rate-limit]]), so the §5.1 gate was not satisfied by it. **Process.** The `major` finding is load-bearing and lands on a number this step reported. `RCCombine.directionality_preserving` was `return True` — a literal, with **zero callers** anywhere in `src/` or `tests/` — while the only tested helper, `is_directionality_preserving(mode)`, compares the *mode name*. But `gate` is `g⊙fwd + (1-g)⊙rc` with a **learned** `g`, and it *becomes* ADR-0005 D15's forbidden order-destroying average at `g ≡ 0.5`; the name cannot see that, and nothing in training prevents it (`weight_decay` applies to `gate_logit` like any other parameter and pulls it toward 0, i.e. toward the mean). So the whole D15 guarantee for the `gate` arm rested on a string plus a nonzero init — the [[gate-clauses-need-re-derivation]] shape exactly: `all(clauses)` catches a clause flipped FALSE and structurally cannot catch one fabricated TRUE. **Outputs.** `stage1_segmenter.py`: `gate_summary()` (a per-channel census read off the live parameter) and `directionality_preserving` re-derived from it; `GATE_MEAN_ATOL` documented as a *numerical-equality* tolerance, explicitly **not** a scientific threshold. `train_stage1.py`: `SCHEMA_VERSION` **3→4**, an `rc_combine` evidence block, and the `rc_directionality_preserved` clause re-derived in `derive_clauses`, registered in `CLAUSE_SCHEMA_VERSION` at `"4"` so the committed schema-3 reports stay valid without back-filling a measurement nobody took; `build_report` now *raises* for a `gate` run handed no census. `ablation_table.py`: a table that fails its own validator is diverted to a `.invalid.json` sibling instead of occupying the canonical, git-committed path.

**The consequence for the measured table, stated plainly.** The four legs ran with `save_checkpoint=False` and their reports record no gate state, so **the `rc_gate` leg's D15 compliance was never measured and cannot be recovered from any retained artifact.** The risk that it actually collapsed is low — the init is asymmetric (`g≈0.622`), a collapse needs all 256 per-channel gates at `0.5` simultaneously, decoupled AdamW decay moves the logit only ~0.35% over 1,160 steps, and the leg still scores Stem_I 0.964 / Terminator 0.925 where an RC-symmetric representation should blur order-dependent identity — but that is an *argument*, not the measurement, and this project does not report a number on the strength of an argument when the constraint is one of its pinned ones. Under the new clause that leg's report re-derives `rc_directionality_preserved` **FALSE** (a `gate` run with no census fails rather than passing on the absence), which is the correct verdict. §7 decision (bioedca, AskUserQuestion 2026-07-29): **re-run the single `rc_gate` leg** so its compliance is measured — ~1.9 GPU-h, taking the P2-12 total to ≈11.8 against ADR-0003 A3's pre-registered ≤ 18, i.e. inside the bound and inside the D8 one-re-submit headroom. That submit is its **own §9.3 ack**.

**A deliberate non-decision, flagged not invented.** The clause answers the **exact structural** question — "is this combination the symmetric average?", true only when *every* channel sits at `0.5`. It is deliberately not a *strength* bound: "asymmetric **enough**" would be a new pinned number, and pinning one is ADR sign-off (§7 item 2), not a constant to invent mid-step. `gate_summary()` therefore reports the degree (`abs_dev_from_half_max`/`_mean`, `n_channels_at_half`) as a measurement a reader can judge.

**Validation.** `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean. Standalone runner in `tbox-finder-data` ([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]): `test_p2_10d_clauses` **46/46** (11 new), `test_ablation_table` **32/32** (2 new), `test_eval_val_clause` 48/48, `test_sizing` 62/62, `test_backbone_registry` 16/16, `test_sbatch_overrides` 18/18. **Three source-sabotage bites, each credited to the test that caught it** and each restored byte-identical by sha256: absence-of-census passes a `gate` run → `test_a_gate_run_that_recorded_no_census_fails_rather_than_passing_on_absence` RED; `<` → `<=` on the channel census → `test_a_gate_collapsed_to_the_symmetric_average_fails` RED; drop the block-mode↔config cross-check → `test_a_block_describing_another_mode_is_not_evidence_about_this_run` RED. The rm-target gate still names only the 8 pre-existing `_KNOWN_DEFECTIVE` files — neither P2-12 sbatch appears. ⚠ **A false green caught in passing:** the first hardened runner crashed on `importlib.util` before executing a single test and reported "0 failures"; silence read as success until the pass counts were demanded. **Decisions.** One existing assertion was *corrected, not weakened*: `test_an_older_schema_report_is_excused_but_not_exempted` asserted `set(BLOCK_FIELD_SCHEMA_VERSION.values()) == {SCHEMA_VERSION}`, a coupling that held only while the ENCODE bump and those fields landed together and that this schema bump falsifies. It now asserts the excuse the docstring actually claims — the baseline predates *every* block field it is excused — which is strictly stronger and survives future bumps. §10.1 N/A. **Commit.** squash **`912508f`** on `main` (PR [#88](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/88)); feature-branch commit on `p2-12-ablations`.

The earlier risk argument was right, and it is now a measurement. Worth noting the gate barely moved from its `sigmoid(0.5)≈0.622` init, so the learned combination is close to a fixed asymmetric mix.

**Result 2 — and this one changes the table.** min-core-F1 **0.9242 → 0.7568** at the *same seed 42, same config, same fold*. Everything upstream is identical: `n_steps` 1160, `world_size` 8, `class_counts` equal, `n_positions` 2,044,769, `n_windows_forwarded` 3,448, `peak_vram_gib` bit-identical, first loss 1.96694 in both; the runs diverge only in accumulated fp nondeterminism (final loss 0.01019 vs 0.00992). **The code change is exonerated** — `gate_summary` is `no_grad`/`detach` at report time, the property had no callers, the clause is report-time. Ranking held; **the argmax decision boundary moved.**

**Why that invalidates the separation verdict.** `min_f1` is a *minimum* over three core elements, so it reports whichever lands worst — and the unstable one decides which rows look bad: baseline / `head_crf` / `size_d256_l4` are all limited by **Specifier** (stable), while `rc_gate` and `size_d118_l4` are limited by **Antiterminator** (the element that just moved 0.167). README and `paper/manuscript.qmd` corrected — both previously asserted the 471k separation as a finding.

**Flagged to P2-13 (calibration).** min-core-F1 under the frozen ADR-0005 D3 reconcile→argmax operator is fragile for Antiterminator precisely because Stage-1 is **uncalibrated** — AUPRC-stable with IoU collapsing is the signature of a threshold effect, not a learning failure. ## Step P2-12 (RESULT — replicates) — 2026-07-30: job 918 replicated the decisive legs; the 471k separation is REAL and replicate-backed, and my run-to-run-variance claim was over-generalised

**Inputs.** SLURM job **918** (`sbatch --array=4,12,13,23 slurm/p2/ablate_stage1.sbatch` at `cec42ef`), the §7-decided replicate array: `baseline` (tid 4), `size_d256_l4` rep2 (12), `size_d118_l4` rep2/rep3 (13, 23). **Process.** All four tasks §9.3-verified — `squeue` terminal, 4/4 `leg_<raw_tid>.OK`, `.err` each 3,249 B of W&B chatter with **0** hits on the scan pattern, each leg's guard echoing its decoded `(leg, replicate)` and axes. Verified **content-based** throughout. Reduced with `--expect-rows 9`.

**Result — the separation returns, on evidence.** Replicates reproduce almost exactly, across independent runs, **different commits** (`a1476b2` → `cec42ef`) and different nodes:

| leg | n | spread | replicate-widened interval | separated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 2 | 0.0006 | [0.9125, 0.9576] | — |
| `size_d118_l4` | 3 | **0.0001** | [0.8581, 0.9047] | **yes** |
| `size_d256_l4` | 2 | 0.0000 | [0.8920, 0.9412] | no |
| `head_crf` | 1 | — | — | withheld |
| `rc_gate` | 1 | — | — | withheld |

0.9047 < 0.9125, so the 471k checkpoint separates downward from the baseline with three replicates at spread 0.0001. `any_axis_separated_from_baseline` is TRUE again — but now it is a *replicated* claim rather than a single-run one, which is the whole point of having gone and measured.

**Correction to the previous stanza, which over-generalised.** I wrote that min-core-F1 carries run-to-run variance the block-bootstrap CI understates ~4×, and rewrote README, the manuscript and the disclosures around that. **The evidence does not support it as a general property.** Every concat-path leg is essentially bit-stable across runs, commits and nodes (≤0.0006). The 0.9242 → 0.7568 disagreement is confined to the **gate** arm — the only leg whose `RCCombine` holds a learned parameter, hence the only one whose backward reduces over batch × length. All four documents are corrected in this commit.

**And a second correction: I over-claimed my own exoneration.** I concluded my code change was exonerated for that swing on bit-identical first loss / `peak_vram` / step counts. That evidence is real but it is *not sufficient*, and the new data sharpens why: the two `rc_gate` runs were at **different commits** (`a1476b2`, `cc04667`), and no two gate runs exist at a single commit. The concat legs being bit-stable across that same commit span rules those commits out **for concat**, not for gate. So two explanations remain live — the gate path is genuinely nondeterministic, or something in the intervening commits moved that leg specifically — and I cannot distinguish them. The disclosure now says exactly that, and the arm's verdict is withheld either way, so the table does not rest on the answer. **Resolvable cheaply** by two gate runs at one commit (~4 GPU-h, total ~19.5, which would breach A3's ≤18 and so needs sign-off) or one gate run at the current commit compared against 906 (~2 GPU-h, total ~17.5, inside the bound).

**Cost — point estimate, later re-derived with bounds (see the correction stanza below).** Job 918: the three small legs are exact at 0.722 / 0.711 / 0.711 GPU-h node-reserved (they ran serially, so consecutive end-times give their walls); the `baseline` leg is **not** exact, because a task's *start* is only known to within the 10-min poll cadence. P2-12 running total ≈ **16 GPU-h** against ADR-0003 A3's pre-registered **≤ 18**. **Outputs.** Four new reports (all `schema_version` 4, all `rc_directionality_preserved` TRUE, all gates passing) · regenerated `reports/p2/ablation_table.json` (9 rows, 0 rejected, `n_separation_assessable` 5) · corrected disclosures, README and `paper/manuscript.qmd` · this stanza.

## Step P2-12 (RESULT — CodeRabbit round 2) — 2026-07-30: two real findings on the final diff, both fixed

**Inputs.** A **real** CodeRabbit CLI review of the whole branch vs `main` (2 findings over 32 files). The GitHub check had reverted to `Review rate limited` on the newest commits — a green check that reviewed nothing ([[coderabbit-fair-usage-rate-limit]]) — so the CLI escalation is what actually satisfied the §5.1 gate. **Process + outputs.** Both findings were valid and both were `major`. **(1)** `eval/backbone_throughput.py` carried the *same* fail-open publication bug already fixed in the reducer: it wrote the canonical `--out` path and only *then* returned 2, so a report failing its own validator would sit at the path the sbatch copies out of scratch as git-committed evidence. Fixed identically — diverted to a `.invalid.json` sibling — so the two entry points now behave the same way rather than one being quietly weaker. **(2)** The leg table grew to five entries while `#SBATCH --array=0-3` stayed, leaving `baseline` (tid 4) unreachable by a default submit. That is not a safety bug (the runtime guard only rejects `tid >= NLEGS`) but it *is* a silent gap between a 5-row table and a 4-task default. Resolved by making the intent explicit rather than by widening the range: the baseline entry is **opt-in by design**, because a default submit must not silently spend ~1.6 GPU-h re-training the very arm whose committed P2-06 point is the reason the baseline row costs 0 new GPU-h. The header now documents the override form (`sbatch --array=4 …`, and the replicate decode), and the test asserts all three facts — default range, 5-entry table with `baseline` last, and the documented override — so the pairing cannot drift again.

## Step P2-12 (RESULT — CodeRabbit round 3) — 2026-07-30: two more real findings fixed, four declined with reasons, and the replicate claim scoped honestly

**Inputs.** A third **real** CodeRabbit CLI review of the branch vs `main` (6 findings, 32 files); the GitHub check stayed `Review rate limited` throughout, so the CLI is again what satisfied §5.1. **Process.** Two findings were real and are fixed; four asked me to **regenerate committed measured reports**, which §10.3 forbids, and rest on misreadings of documented design — declined **with reasons recorded**, not silently.

**Fixed (1) — the baseline row was the one row nothing validated.** `artifact_problems` re-derived `separated_from_baseline` for every row *except* `is_baseline` ones, which it skipped. Since that verdict is structurally fixed at `None`, skipping made it the only place a fabricated value could survive — the P1-15/P1-16 shape again, one layer in. It is now validated explicitly (a baseline row carrying any non-`None` verdict is an error).

**Fixed (2) — and this one is scientific, not mechanical.** CodeRabbit observed that every replicate holds **seed 42**. That is correct and deliberate — the seed is part of the ADR-0003 A3 pinned protocol, so changing it is an ADR decision, not a reducer choice — but it means my replicates measure **run-to-run determinism at a fixed seed**, which is near-total (hence the ~0 spreads), and **not seed variance**. A different seed is an equally valid draw of the same procedure, so the replicate-widened intervals are barely wider than the single-run CIs and the separation verdict does **not** account for initialisation. The disclosure now says so in terms, and instructs the reader to take `separated_from_baseline` as *"separated at the pinned seed"*, not *"separated in general"*. This materially narrows what the 471k finding claims, which is the honest reading rather than the flattering one.

**Declined, with reasons.** (a) `warm_start_loaded: true` beside a null `warm_start` block is not an inconsistency: `_warm_start_ok`'s own docstring pins it — "when `init_from_checkpoint` is unset the clause is satisfied by the *recorded absence* of a warm start… a fresh build must say so". (b) `diagnostics.pinned: false` is a deliberate honesty field meaning *this config is not ADR-pinned*, not *the backbone bypassed the registry*; every leg resolved through the allow-list with a **measured** parameter count, which the report carries. (c)/(d) `git_dirty` naming `data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet` is the documented `_DATA_STAGING_PREFIXES=("data/",)` allowance — this cluster has no git-lfs, so the split table *must* be rsync'd and is unavoidably dirty; "re-run from a clean worktree" is not available there, and the sbatch already sha256-verifies that file against its committed LFS pointer before any GPU time. The suggestion's better half — record that digest **in the report** rather than only in the job log — is a genuine improvement, but it can only take effect by re-running every leg, and back-filling it into committed reports would forge a measurement. Logged as a follow-up for the next training step rather than faked here.

**Validation.** `ruff`/`black` clean; `test_ablation_table` **37/37** (2 new). **Two source-sabotage bites**, both credited by name and restored byte-identical. ⚠ **A non-biting verdict caught and corrected:** the first attempt at the disclosure bite reported "restored byte-identical" and a green suite — but the `sed` anchor never existed (black had reflowed the string concatenation), so the mutation was a **no-op** and the green proved nothing ([[sabotage-restores-masked-by-pycache]] class: a non-bite is only a result if the sabotage provably changed the bytes). Re-run with the mutation asserted and the file hash shown to change, it bites correctly. §10.1 N/A. **Commit.** squash **`912508f`** on `main` (PR [#88](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/88)); feature-branch commit on `p2-12-ablations`.

**Why.** A read-back of the P2-12 stanzas before closing the step, prompted by the user. Three defects in my own record, none of which change the scientific result but two of which change what a reader would conclude.

The heading now flags the supersession and a block quote at the top of that stanza names all three reversals, with the original text kept verbatim beneath. Erasing it would destroy the record of what was believed when, which is the part of a lab notebook that has value.

**(2) The GPU-h total was a point estimate presented as if measured, and its headroom was used for a decision.** I wrote "≈16.2 GPU-h … with ~1.8 left, which is one more small-leg pair but *not* a second gate leg plus slack", and in the same breath proposed a ~2 GPU-h gate run as "inside the bound". |---|---|---|

| 906 (rc_gate) | 1.21 – 2.55 | start known only to a 10-min window |
