## Step P2-13 — 2026-07-30: the Stage-1 calibration machinery, and the measured finding that there is almost nothing to calibrate

**Inputs.** The round-0 production checkpoint (`data/processed/checkpoints/stage1_production/stage1.pt`, SLURM job 671 / P2-09 `082f8c7`, DVC-tracked and materialised locally), the P2-06a `selection_val` inner rung (830 records / 469 clusters) via `window_dataset.load_selection_val_records`, and the frozen binned-ECE estimator `metrics.binned_ece` (15 equal-mass debiased bins, ADR-0005 D11).

**Process.** Four things this step needs were **unpinned** — verified absent from `PRD.md` and all six ADRs, not merely unfound: the calibration *axis* for a per-nucleotide 8-class segmenter (D11 pins its estimator *"on the positive-class posterior"*, wording written for Stage-2's binary head), the *parameterisation* (one shared T vs per-class T), the *optimiser*, and — the load-bearing one — *which fold*, since D11's "disjoint calibration split" is a phrase that occurs exactly once in the PRD and the `calib` column it names is carved at **P3-02**, not here. Those went to the user as a §7 stop with a drafted amendment; **ADR-0005 A11** was signed 2026-07-30 and pins: the per-nt 8-class axis with a **per-class one-vs-rest** read; **one shared scalar T** (the method of the arXiv:1706.04599 paper D11 already cites); an **exact convex 1-D solve** in `β = 1/T` rather than LBFGS; T applied **before** the frozen D3+A3 reconciliation operator; and a **seeded whole-cluster halving of `selection_val`** — fit on half A, read on half B — with the shipped disclosure that this is *not* D11's split and that **no T from this step is shipped**. Landed as `src/tbox_finder/calib/temperature.py` (+ `metrics.reliability_bins`, promoted out of `binned_ece` so the plotted curve and the reported number are one arithmetic; the committed hand-computed expectations in `tests/ml/test_eval_gate.py` reproduce **bit-exactly** across that refactor) and run locally: 415 records fitted, 415 read, ≈50 min wall on the laptop 4060 (0.30 GiB peak VRAM; the 200-replicate cluster-blocked bootstrap over the pure-Python estimator, not the GPU, is what costs).

**Outputs.** `reports/p2/calibration.json` + `reports/p2/calibration_figure_data.json` + `figures/calib/reliability_selection_val.png`; `src/tbox_finder/calib/{__init__,temperature}.py`; `tests/unit/test_temperature.py` (66 checks, torch-free); ADR-0005 **A11**.

**Result — the number is T = 0.989587** (β = 1.010523; known to ±5.8e-5, a bound re-derivable from the recorded bracket and iteration count), fitted on 1,778,688 per-window positions, moving the per-position NLL 0.017839 → 0.017836. That is a **1 % correction, i.e. essentially none**: the Stage-1 posteriors are already near-calibrated on this fold. Per-class one-vs-rest ECE on the read half (1,018,693 nt / 176 clusters) is 0.0071 background, 0.0019 Stem I, 0.0010 Stem II, 0.0013 Stem III, 0.0014 Terminator, 0.0008 Antiterminator, 0.0001 Specifier, 0.0002 Discriminator — every value moves by ≤ 1.7e-5 under T, in **both** directions. **These are not GATE-2 numbers** (wrong fold, wrong phase, and GATE-2 is graded at P3 exit on the P3-02 carve); quoting them against the 0.05 bar would be a category error.

**Two findings worth more than the headline number.**

**(1) A single shared T is structurally the wrong instrument for what is actually miscalibrated here.** For every non-background class, **80–93 %** of read-half positions sit in bins whose mean posterior is below 1e-4 — the trivially-easy "model says ≈0, truth is ≈0" mass — so the per-class ECE is small largely because the task is imbalanced. The informative bin is the top one, and there the model is consistently **over**-confident: Stem I predicts 0.599 against an observed 0.570, Terminator 0.188 against 0.167, Antiterminator 0.182 against 0.169. Background, at 91.2 % prevalence, predicts 0.99992 against an observed 1.00000 — *under*-confident. A shared scalar T must trade those against each other, and the pooled NLL is 91 % background, so it lands at T slightly **below** 1 — sharpening, the opposite of what the rare classes want. This is a measured argument for testing **vector (per-class) scaling** at P3, and it is exactly the choice A11 declined to pin without evidence.

**(2) P2-12's flag is answered, and the answer is "no", for a reason worth recording.** P2-12 asked whether temperature scaling stabilises the Antiterminator min-core-F1 fragility under the frozen D3 arg-max operator. It does not — but **not** because scaling is arg-max-invariant. A single T preserves each *window's* arg-max exactly, yet the D3+A3 operator averages *probabilities* across overlapping windows, so re-tempering can move the **reconciled** arg-max wherever coverage ≥ 2, which describes **664,399** of the read half's 1,018,693 positions. The mechanism is live; its magnitude at T = 0.9896 is **2 positions** (0.0002 %), and Antiterminator boundary IoU moves 0.91739 → 0.91732. So the fragility must be addressed at the operating point (P2-14) or by a form that can move an arg-max on purpose — not by this. GATE-4 stays graded on the uncalibrated posterior.

**Validation.** Unit tier **66/66** green (torch-free, so it runs in CI's no-torch env) via the standalone runner (`[[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]`); `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean at CI-exact versions. The `binned_ece` refactor is **bit-exact**: 130 old-vs-new comparisons with 0 differences, and the committed `tests/fixtures/eval_gate_sample/expected.json` values (`ece_plugin` 0.18163780627134027, `ece_debiased` 0.10702781774830165) reproduce to the last bit. **Four source-sabotage bites**, each with the mutation's byte change shown and each restored byte-identically: equal-width instead of equal-mass binning → RED; deleting the exact `β → ∞` degeneracy guard → RED; deleting the sampled-gradient bracket guard → RED; deleting the fit-half re-derivation → the inversion test RED. The artifact's own gate re-derives all seven clauses from the report (including re-cutting the halves from the recorded cluster→size map) and passes. ⚠ **A non-biting verdict caught and fixed mid-step:** the first perfect-accuracy test matched *either* degeneracy message, so deleting the exact-limit guard left the suite green — the sampled-gradient branch caught the same input. Both tests now match their own message, and each guard was re-sabotaged separately to prove it (`[[sabotage-attribution-must-name-the-test]]`).

**Decisions.** ADR-0005 **A11** (signed; five pins + the disclosure set). Two defects the work surfaced and fixed: the fit's `|grad| ≤ tol` stopping rule read an **underflowed** gradient tail as stationarity and would have certified an arbitrary T on a perfectly-accurate fold — replaced by the exact `β → ∞` limit `Σ(max_c z − z_label)`, which cannot underflow; and `imp.md`'s P2-09 status marker still read `☐ todo` for a step merged as PR #61 (`082f8c7`) — corrected in place, with a note that the P2-00…P2-08 and P2-10a markers are stale the same way and that `TODO.md` is the authoritative record. **§10.1 evidence gate:** the one cited methodological claim (single-parameter temperature scaling as the multi-class post-hoc form) carries arXiv:1706.04599, already D11's citation; the convexity of `NLL(β)` and the monotonicity of `logits/T` are derivations, not empirical claims, and the arg-max behaviour *through* the averaging operator was left as a measurement rather than asserted. **Commit.** squash **`ae9288b`** on `main` (PR [#90](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/90)); feature-branch commit on `p2-13-calibration`.

## Step P2-13 (CodeRabbit round 1) — 2026-07-30: four findings, three of them real defects, and a reproducibility fact the re-run exposed

**Inputs.** A real CodeRabbit CLI review of the branch against `main` (4 findings, 9 files reviewed). The GitHub check again reported only `Review rate limited` — a green check that reviewed nothing (`[[coderabbit-fair-usage-rate-limit]]`), so the CLI is what satisfied §5.1.

**Fixed (1) — the fit could emit a report its own validator rejects.** The bisection accepted `|grad| <= grad_tol` **or** a collapsed bracket as convergence. On the width path it returned `converged = True` carrying a gradient larger than `grad_tol` — exactly the clause `validate_report` checks. That is the P2-12 `build_report`-vs-`validate_report` shape one layer in, and the two exits now cannot disagree: only the stationarity residual certifies a fit, and a bracket that collapses first **raises**. The committed artifact is unaffected — it converged on the gradient (|grad| = 1.53 ≤ 1.78 at iteration 24), which is re-derivable from the recorded `bracket` + `n_iterations`.

**Fixed (2) — the validator could die instead of reporting.** `validate_report`'s contract is *"total — returns problems, never raises"*, but it did `float(r.get("weight", 0.0))` and `r["debiased_gap"]` over reliability rows and `per_class[e]["ece"]` over core elements, all of which raise on a malformed artifact. A validator that crashes reports nothing, which is strictly worse than one that reports a problem. Rows are shape-checked before any arithmetic, and the core-element re-derivation is guarded the way `read_is_out_of_sample` already was.

**Fixed (3) — a NaN posterior would have produced a plausible-looking ECE.** The estimator sorts by posterior, so a NaN or out-of-range value sorts somewhere arbitrary and returns a number. The check lives in `per_class_reliability`, **not** in `metrics.binned_ece`: that kernel is frozen and golden-locked, and a per-call scan of its `Sequence` inputs would run once per class per bootstrap replicate (3,200 times here). One vectorised numpy check per read covers every value this module hands it, at O(N) instead of O(N × 3200).

**Fixed (4) — the artifact recorded an absolute `/home/<user>/…` checkpoint path.** Unresolvable for any reviewer of a public repo. Now relativised — against the running checkout **and** its main checkout, because this step runs from a `.claude/worktrees/` worktree while the DVC-tracked inputs are materialised only in the main checkout, so relativising against the worktree alone would have fallen back to absolute for every real input and the guard would never have fired where it matters.

**The re-run exposed something the first run could not have shown.** Regenerating the artifact under the fixed code reproduced **T = 0.989586718 bit-for-bit**, and every count identical — arg-max changes 2, coverage ≥ 2 at 664,399, the cluster halves, `gate4_core_min_f1` 0.956043956 — but the artifact was **not** byte-identical: per-class ECEs agree to ≤ 3e-8 relative, the largest disagreement anywhere in the read is **4.5e-6** relative on a bin edge, and `temperature.grad_at_solution` — a cancelling sum over ~1.8e6 terms — differs by **2.7e-4** relative. The cause is the GPU forward, not this module: the Mamba/CUDA kernels reduce in a run-dependent order, so the logits differ in their last bits. The fit and the halving are exactly deterministic; the *measurement they consume* is not. This now ships as a ninth report disclosure carrying those measured bounds, so a future reader diffs by re-derivation and tolerance rather than for equality — and the committed artifact is the one the shipped code produced, not the pre-fix one.

**Validation.** Unit **74/74** (8 new: the width-termination refusal, the posterior-range guard with four corruption modes, the worktree-aware path rule, and five malformed-report shapes that used to raise inside the validator). **Four further source-sabotage bites**, each with its byte change shown and restored byte-identically: restoring width-only convergence → RED; dropping the posterior-range check → RED; dropping the row shape-check → 3 RED; dropping path relativisation → RED. `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean; CI green on the parent commit (lint, pytest, snakemake). §10.1 N/A. **Commit.** squash **`ae9288b`** on `main` (PR [#90](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/90)); feature-branch commit on `p2-13-calibration`.

## Step P2-13 (CodeRabbit round 2) — 2026-07-30: the diversion my own round-1 fix made incomplete, and a test that would have been vacuous exactly where it runs

**Inputs.** A second real CodeRabbit CLI review of the branch (2 findings, both real).

**Fixed (1) — an invalid report was diverted but its figure data was not.** Round 1 established that a malformed report never lands on the step's path (`calibration.invalid.json`). But the reliability diagram is rendered **from `calibration_figure_data.json`**, and that file kept its canonical name — so a run whose report was refused would still leave a plottable curve under the good name, beside a report marked invalid. ## Step P2-14 (ENCODE) — 2026-07-30: the gate had no population, and building one cost a second training run

**Inputs.** ADR-0004 D6 (the gated statistic + the 0.80 floor), the committed split table
`data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet`, the shipped production checkpoint's own
training report `reports/p2/train_stage1_production.json`, the P0-21 crystal fixture
`tests/fixtures/pdb_element_extents/`, and the pinned kernels already in `metrics.py`.

**The finding that shaped the step.** D6 gates *"the in-distribution homology-clustered
(genus-stratified) split"*, and **no such population is held out from the checkpoint D6
grades**. The shipped scanner trained on the full D5 fold — `selection_val_excluded: false`,
`n_records: 8303` in its own report — so, measured on the committed table: scheme-A `test`
is **1,204 / 2,353 (51.2 %)** inside the training stream; of the 1,149 that are not, **786**
are designated leave-one-order-out records (the generalization arm D6 does *not* gate); and
the 353 that are neither are the clade-crossing (271) and no-clade (82) residues `splits.py`
marks *never scored*. `selection_val` is both inside the training stream and the fold the
P2-06 sweep selected γ/lr/α on. Every candidate population was disqualified for a different
reason, and the disqualifications are measurements, not readings of prose.

**Process.** That went to the user as a §7 stop with the four options costed. The signed
answer (2026-07-30, AskUserQuestion) is **ADR-0004 A6**: grade a **GATE-4 eval twin** —
the production protocol with one changed override, `exclude_gate4_eval=true` — on
`gate4_eval`, the scheme-A `test` records **inside** `nested_train`. Measured with the
shipped loader: **1,201 records / 1,029 clusters / 154 genera / 15 orders / 2,976,259 nt**
(3 records excluded as shorter than one window, counted not padded), and the carve is
cluster-closed — withholding it costs the twin exactly its own 1,204 records, **8,303 →
7,099**, nothing lost unscored. The **shipped** checkpoint stays the full-fold one, so the
twin's grade is a *conservative* proxy for it: PRD §10.1's two-run split, now with a
mechanism behind the phrase.

**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/eval/gate4.py` (`score_records` — the tile → forward →
reconcile → per-block-confusion loop **promoted** out of `train_stage1.evaluate_selection_val`,
which now delegates to it, so the arithmetic a config is *selected* under and the arithmetic
GATE-4 *grades* under are one implementation; `compute_gate4`; `pdb_label_noise_ceiling`;
`build_report`; `gate4_problems`); `window_dataset.{gate4_eval_cluster_ids,
load_gate4_eval_records, gate4_eval_problems, load_loo_holdout_records, record_order}` +
`load_corpus_records(exclude_gate4_eval=)`; `train_stage1.exclude_gate4_eval` +
`conf/train/stage1.yaml`'s key (the job-669 struct-mode lesson); `metrics.{class_runs,
iou_from_confusion, specifier_exact_codon_detection}`; `workflow/rules/eval.smk::gate4_stage1`;
`slurm/p2/train_gate4_twin.sbatch`; ADR-0004 **A6**.

**Three things the design refuses to assume.** (i) The gate **re-derives** `min_f1` from the
per-element F1s rather than trusting the reported value, and re-derives `passes` from the
floor — a copied statistic is exactly what a mean-instead-of-min bug would produce. (ii) It
refuses to grade a checkpoint that cannot **prove** it is a twin: the twin property is read
from the training run's own report (`fold_scope == "gate4_twin_train"` *and*
`n_gate4_eval_excluded > 0`, the **measured** exclusion, not the requested flag) and bound to
the checkpoint bytes by sha256 through the provenance sidecar. A flag that was set but
carved nothing fails the clause. (iii) The **9-PDB ceiling is re-derived, not restated**: 0 of

gate measures — and the clause flips on its own if a future deposition resolves them.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 1) — 2026-07-30: five findings, three real, and one whose stated failure mode was wrong while the defect underneath was not

**Inputs.** A real CodeRabbit CLI review of `p2-14-gate4` against `main` — 5 findings (2 major,

`pdb_label_noise_ceiling` re-derives `estimable` from the fixture's own resolved-class map
specifically so a tenth deposition flips it without a code change — and then the prose beside
that derivation said *"0 of the 9"* and *"the floor stays 0.80"* as string literals. Those are
reported numbers in a shipped artifact: after a fixture grows or ADR-0004 re-signs δ they keep
asserting nine depositions and a 0.80 floor, and a wrong number reads exactly like a right one
(§10.3). Both now come from the evidence — the count from the fixture's `entries`, the floor
from `power.GATE4_F1_FLOOR` — with an honest degradation ("the depositions supplied") when the
fixture carries no `entries` block at all, rather than an f-string rendering `None`.

**Fixed (2) — one statistic, two exact routes, and nothing compared them.** Every gated number
has two routes in `eval/gate4.py`: the pooled `metrics` kernels walking ~3.0M positions, and
the `*_from_confusion` re-association of the per-block `(8, 3)` sufficient statistics. The
identity is exact, and `test_confusion_route_reproduces_the_pinned_f1_and_iou_kernels` pins it
**on a fixture** — but `compute_gate4` computed `gated.min_f1` pooled and
`gated.block_bootstrap_ci.point` from confusions and never checked them against each other, so
on the run that actually ships a divergence would have been published as two contradictory
headline values for one statistic. The check is now a pure kernel,
`cross_route_disagreements`, called on the real run and unit-tested directly: it compares all
eight per-class F1s, all eight IoUs and the gated minimum, and names each disagreement. It is
NaN-aware by construction — `nan == nan` is False and NaN is the honest score for an element no
position exercises, so a naive equality check would have fired on every clean run and been
turned off. No reported number changes (the identity is exact); what changes is that a
divergence now raises instead of shipping.

clones `train_production.sbatch`, including its DONE marker, flock lock and `%j` SLURM logs —
and arrived with none of the four ignored, which is the P2-10d′-e defect one job later: a
`git add -A` on the sacrificial cluster checkout commits a lock file and torchrun chatter where
the sibling jobs all ignore their own. ⚠ **The reviewer's stated mechanism was wrong** — it
claimed `_provenance_complete` would read the lock as dirty state, but `train_stage1.py:852`
snapshots `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=no`, so untracked run signals are
invisible to that gate. The hygiene defect underneath was real regardless. Rather than copy
`test_train_production_signals.py` into a second per-file version — the arrangement where one
copy gets fixed and the other ships the bug — its four cases are now parametrised over a
registry of DDP training sbatches, plus a new case asserting the registry names paths the
sbatch **actually writes**, so a drifted entry cannot make the other four self-certify.

and `splits` are declared but passed to no CLI flag, which the review read as Snakemake
tracking files the command does not read. It reads all three:
`eval.gate4` → `window_dataset.load_gate4_eval_records`, whose `context_parquet` /
`labels_parquet` / `split_table` default to exactly those paths. Dropping them would stop the
DAG rebuilding GATE-4 when the corpus, labels, or — decisively — the split table that *defines*
the graded population (ADR-0004 A6) changes. Kept, with the reasoning written into the rule so
the next reader does not "clean up" a staleness guard.

**Refuted (5) — the hardcoded `CONDA_SH`.** The suggestion was to derive it from `$HOME`. The

also break the property the twin exists to have: byte-for-byte identical to
`train_production.sbatch` apart from the single `exclude_gate4_eval=true` override, without

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 2) — 2026-07-30: the same defect one block over, and a validator that died on the artifacts it exists to catch

from the evidence they describe — `twin.n_training_records`, `scope.phylum_counts` /
`scope.n_records`, `reported_non_gated.pdb_label_noise_ceiling`, `power.GATE4_F1_FLOOR` — with

ceiling *becomes* estimable that still refuses to move the floor without ADR-0004 re-sign-off.

named constant because it describes a **different artifact** that no key of this run
re-derives. Note the phylum share is now the share of the graded population
(`scope.n_records`), not the pre-window-filter 1,204 no key of the report carries — the
derivable number rather than the one that reads better. This is r1's δ-governance finding
recurring one block over, which is the P2-13 r2 shape exactly: my own round-1 fix was

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 3) — 2026-07-30: a deliverable no non-Python reader could parse, and a clause bound to the wrong bytes

**Inputs.** A third CodeRabbit CLI review after the r2 commit — 3 findings, all flagged major,
all in the ENCODE code rather than in the review fixes. Two real, one refuted from the source.

**Fixed (1) — the GATE-4 report would not have been valid JSON.** `main` wrote it with a plain
`json.dumps`, which emits bare `NaN` / `Infinity` tokens. Python's own `json.loads` reads those
back, which is exactly why this survives every Python-side check — but they are not JSON, and
`jq`, JavaScript, R's `jsonlite`, Go and Rust all reject the **entire file**. This is not a
hypothetical for GATE-4, which produces NaN *by design*: an element no position exercises
scores NaN so it cannot silently certify the gate, `iou_from_confusion` is NaN on an empty
union (Stem III and Discriminator can easily be absent from 1,201 records), and
`block_bootstrap_ci` is NaN below two blocks. The phase-exit deliverable of a public repo
would have been unparseable for reviewers while looking clean from inside the pipeline. Fixed
with `json_safe` — the `eval/backbone_throughput.py` idiom already in this package — mapping
non-finite floats to `null`, converting numpy scalars (`np.int64` does not subclass `int`),
and deliberately *not* stringifying unknown types so `json.dumps` still raises on them rather
than writing a plausible-looking value. `allow_nan=False` follows as the belt: it can only fire
if the sanitiser missed something. Nothing re-validates the written file — `gate4_problems`
runs on the in-memory report inside `compute_gate4`, before the write — so the NaN semantics
the gate depends on are untouched. The test asserts on the serialised **text**, because
`json.loads` accepts `NaN` and a round-trip test would have passed either way.

**Fixed (2) — the identity clause was bound to whichever sidecar entry came first.**
`twin_evidence` read the provenance sidecar's `outputs` map by iterating and taking the first
value. `checkpoint_identity_verified` is the clause that binds the report to the checkpoint
*bytes* — the thing standing between GATE-4 and grading a checkpoint that is not the twin — and
"some output of some sidecar" is not evidence of the artifact it names. Today every training
sidecar records exactly one output, so this was latent, and the existing clause makes a
mismatch fail **loudly** rather than pass, which bounds the live cost at a spurious refusal
after a ~16 GPU-h run rather than a fabricated pass. Now a lookup: the graded checkpoint's path
first, its basename second, a lone entry third, and `None` — a refusal the clause judges —
when two entries share a basename or several exist with no path to disambiguate.

**Refuted (3) — `exclude_selection_val` + `exclude_gate4_eval` do not make the selection bucket
drift.** The concern was that the selection carve should be drawn from the non-GATE-4 remainder,
or the two sets validated disjoint. Read from the source: `load_corpus_records` computes
`val_clusters` from `_training_fold_cluster_sizes(rows)` and `gate4_clusters` from
`gate4_eval_cluster_ids(rows)` — **both from the same unfiltered rows** — and then applies them
as independent membership filters in one pass. So the seeded draw never sees a shrunken pool,
and an overlapping record is simply excluded once. Deriving the selection bucket from the
remainder, as suggested, is the change that would introduce the defect: it would silently
re-cut the very fold the P2-06 sweep chose its winner on. No shipped config sets both flags in
any case (the twin sets `exclude_gate4_eval` alone). Rather than change the code, the property
is now pinned by a test that builds a fixture where the two derivations *provably* differ, then
asserts from the source that the shipped loader uses the non-drifting one — so a future
"cleanup" toward the reviewer's suggestion goes red.

**Validation.** Unit **90/90** on `test_gate4_metrics.py` (12 further new: NaN/Infinity
serialisation asserted on the text, numpy-scalar conversion + loud failure on unknown types,
seven provenance-lookup cases including not-first / ambiguous-basename, the end-to-end twin
identity check both ways, and the carve non-drift pin). Full local `tests/unit` + `tests/golden`
+ `tests/ml`: **2,973 passed / 13 failed**, all 13 the same `ImportError` for `pyarrow` /
`mamba_ssm` absent from the only local env carrying pytest — unchanged from the r1 baseline and
touching nothing in this diff. `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean; `snakemake --lint` clean.
**Two further source-sabotage bites, restored sha256-verified:** dropping `json_safe`'s
non-finite branch → 2 RED; restoring the first-entry provenance lookup → 4 RED, including the
`not-first` and `ambiguous-basename` cases by name.

**Nothing was graded this session.** No twin exists, `reports/p2/gate4.json` is not written, and
no GATE-4 number is claimed. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); feature-branch commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (RUN + RESULT) — 2026-07-31: GATE-4 passes in-distribution at 0.952, and the same checkpoint reads 0.72 macro across held-out orders

**Inputs.** `slurm/p2/train_gate4_twin.sbatch` at commit `1128974` on the cluster checkout; the
five staged parquets, each verified by the run against its committed pointer before any GPU
time — including `data/processed/splits/split_assignments.parquet` at sha256
`6388ba19328811fa81d2d5b84a58643674934b4286581d8eff9df2e2cefba029`, equal to its committed
git-LFS pointer. **Process.** Job **957** was submitted 2026-07-30T15:35:59Z and then sat
**PENDING for 15.3 hours** — not a queue wait but a structural one: both GPU nodes were fully
allocated to four `cryosparc` jobs at `gres/gpu:a4000:4` each, **twelve more cryosparc jobs
were queued ahead at UNLIMITED walltime**, and job 957 carried `Priority=1`, the floor. Every
4-GPU block that freed went to the next cryosparc job; an 8-GPU-on-one-node request can only
start when a whole node empties *and* that queue is dry, which is why SLURM reported
`StartTime=2027-07-30T14:55:15` — its one-year placeholder for *unschedulable*. The one change
that would have made it fit — dropping to four GPUs — was rejected rather than taken: the
trainer has no gradient accumulation, so world size 8 → 4 moves the global batch 64 → 32 and
re-slices the `rank::world_size` draw stream, and the twin's entire evidential value is that it
differs from the shipped production run by **exactly one override**. The user decision
(2026-07-31) was to keep it queued unchanged; node `two` freed at 06:53Z and the job ran
**≈2 h 11 m** (Σ rank-0 step time 7,494.9 s = 2.082 h over 12,200 steps, ≈17.5 GPU-h
node-reserved against the ≈16.1 estimate). **Outputs.**
`data/processed/checkpoints/stage1_gate4_twin/`
(DVC, `stage1_gate4_twin.dvc`, dir-md5 `7869eec10539f4d3172ef9f4c3b28496`)
+ `reports/p2/train_stage1_gate4_twin.json` + `reports/p2/gate4.json`.

**§9.3 step-8 verification — artifact-based (sacct off), all green.** `squeue -j 957` empty
(rc=0); `train_stage1_gate4_twin.DONE` present; checkpoint + `provenance.json` present; and the
run's own publish guard printed `twin-ok fold_scope=gate4_twin_train n_gate4_eval_excluded=1204
n_records=7099` — the pinned 8,303 → 7,099 carve, re-derived from the run's own report rather
than asserted. The `.err` is **expected non-empty** for this job (32 lines of `trust_remote_code`
/ torchrun / W&B-offline chatter) and was therefore *scanned*, not zero-gated: zero
`Traceback`/`Error`/`CUDA`/`assert`/`Killed` hits. The retrieved `stage1.pt` hashes to
`0140a8a32f82f49fec9ddf047de6590a130cd51cd5feab01086ed89032944a29`, **equal** to the sha256 its
provenance sidecar independently recorded — the report is bound to the checkpoint bytes, not to
a filename. The run's provenance shows `git_sha 1128974…` with `git_dirty_paths` = the staged
split table alone, the documented `_DATA_STAGING_PREFIXES` allowance.

**Validation — GATE-4 PASS.** Minimum per-nucleotide class F1 over {Stem I, Specifier,
Antiterminator} = **0.951776** against the ADR-0004 D6 floor **0.80**, on the ADR-0004 A6
`gate4_eval` population: 1,201 records / 1,029 homology clusters / 15 orders / 2,976,259
positions / 5,102 reconciled windows. Cluster-blocked bootstrap 95 % CI **[0.9426, 0.9605]**
(1,029 blocks, 2,000 resamples), so the floor is cleared by the *lower* bound, not just the
point. Per element: Stem I 0.9749, Antiterminator 0.9697, **Specifier 0.9518 — the minimum, and
the statistic**. The population is disjoint from what the graded checkpoint saw, and the report
proves it rather than assuming it: **0** shared cluster ids and **0** shared record ids with the
twin's 7,099-record training fold, 0 records from the designated leave-one-order-out holdout,
0 outside `nested_train`.

**Reported, explicitly non-gated.** Micro F1 0.9929, macro 0.9550. Boundary IoU per core
element — Stem I 0.951, Antiterminator 0.941, Specifier 0.908 — computed through the frozen
ADR-0005 D3+A3 log-mean-exp operator, which is what makes them element extents rather than
512-grid artefacts. Non-core: Discriminator 0.974 / IoU 0.949, Stem II 0.954 / 0.913,
Terminator 0.939 / 0.885, **Stem III 0.880 / 0.786** — the weakest class by both measures, and
correctly outside the gate. AUPRC spans 0.952 (Stem III) to 0.9999 (background). Specifier
exact-3-nt-codon detection: **89.79 %** exact (1,046 / 1,165 scorable), 91.85 % right-length,
98.71 % overlapping; 36 records are unscorable and are reported by reason rather than dropped
(26 have no Specifier in truth, 10 have a truth Specifier of length 1, 2, or 8).

**The 9-PDB label-noise ceiling refuses, and the refusal is the finding.** C is **not
estimable**: Antiterminator and Specifier resolve to a residue extent in **0 of the 9**
depositions (Stem I in 5, Stem II in 1), so no cross-source per-nt F1 over the gated elements
exists. D6's δ-recalibration path — floor := a documented function of C — is therefore
**closed**, and the floor stands at 0.80 as written. An N ≤ 9 crystal ceiling must not
one-directionally lower the bar, and here it cannot even try.

**The number that is not the headline.** The leave-one-order-out read, over 21,030,072
positions / 35,431 windows and macro-averaged across **30** held-out orders per ADR-0005 D5,
gives Antiterminator **0.765**, Stem I **0.721**, Specifier **0.715** — every core element well
under the in-distribution 0.95, with per-order minima at or near zero. That gap is the honest
shape of the project: GATE-4 grades *segmentation quality on the in-distribution reference*
(ADR-0004 D6), and the generalization claim PRD §12:241 makes is graded at GATE-1 / P4 on
exactly this axis. Reporting the 0.952 without the 0.72 beside it would be the paper's central
error, so both ship in the same report and the same manuscript paragraph.

**Decisions.** No threshold moved, no tier changed. Five disclosures ship *inside* `gate4.json`,
each derived from the run's own evidence rather than typed in: the graded artefact is the
**twin**, not the shipped checkpoint (which trained on all 8,303 D5 records including this
population, so it has no in-distribution holdout at all — the twin saw strictly fewer records,
making 0.952 a **conservative proxy**, PRD §10.1's two-run split); the population is **98.7 %
Firmicutes** (1,185/1,201), which is what the corpus leaves after the order-holdout is removed,
not a sampling choice; the LOO read is never gated here; the grade is on the **uncalibrated**
posterior (ADR-0005 A11 Pin 4 — P2-13's T = 0.9896 is machinery, not shipped); and C is not
estimable. **Still open:** the staged split table's sha256 is verified by the run and printed to
its own log, but is still not a *field* in the training report — back-filling it into a
completed run's report would forge a measurement, so that follow-up stays open for the next
training leg. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); feature-branch commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 5) — 2026-07-31: the cost knobs could certify, and the truncated number was the flattering one

**Inputs.** `coderabbit review --agent -t committed --base main` over `3c6162c`, the RESULT
commit. **Process.** One finding, major, and real. The knobs `--max-records`,
`--loo-max-records` and `--no-loo` exist to make a cheap run possible, but nothing stopped a
cheap run from *certifying*: every clause in `gate4_problems` survives truncation unharmed,
because an 8-record prefix of a disjoint population is still disjoint, still `gate4_eval`, and
still has ≥ 2 blocks. The LOO clause was worse than merely silent — written
`isinstance(loo, Mapping) and loo and loo.get("gated") is not False`, it went **vacuous exactly
when `--no-loo` removed the evidence** D6 requires alongside the gate, the
[[clauses-must-guard-emptiness]] shape this project has now hit four times. I confirmed the
defect by running the **committed pre-fix bytes** rather than reasoning about them
([[verify-the-line-you-ship]]): `--max-records 8 --no-loo` wrote `is_science: true`,
`gated: true`, `passes: true`, `min_f1 = 0.9864` over **eight** records with
`loo_holdout: null`, to the default `--out` — which is the phase-exit deliverable path. Note
the direction: the truncated number is **higher** than the real 0.9518, so the failure mode
flatters.

**Outputs.** Three clauses in `gate4_problems`, total and evidence-guarded like the rest:
`scope.full_fold` must be True, `scope.max_records` must be None, and `loo_holdout` must be
**present** — firing on absence, not only on a wrong value — with `loo_holdout.scope.full_fold`
True. No new refusal machinery was needed: `compute_gate4` already raises on any problem
*before* writing, so an incomplete run now emits no file at all, and that is precisely what
makes `build_report`'s hardcoded `is_science: True` honest rather than decorative. Post-fix the
same command exits 1 naming all three problems and writes nothing; `reports/p2/gate4.json` is
byte-untouched.

**Validation.** 98/98 standalone (was 90) — the local pytest env is py3.10 and dies importing
`datetime.UTC`, so the suite runs through a stub-`pytest` harness in the py3.12 env
([[no-local-pytest-env-validate-standalone]]). Seven new cases: five sabotages of the report
and, deliberately, **a regression test that runs the CURRENT validator over the REAL committed
report** — adding a clause is exactly how a previously-valid measured artifact silently becomes
uncertifiable ([[new-gate-clause-invalidates-old-reports]]), and that cannot be fixed by
editing the report, because re-running is the only honest way to change a measurement. **Seven
source-sabotage bites, each RED by name:** disabling the two scope clauses reds cases 27/28/29;
restoring the *exact* pre-fix LOO block reds 30/31/32/33. My first attempt at that second
sabotage left a malformed `else:` and killed the cases on an `AttributeError` instead of the
named assertion — a bite for the wrong reason is not a bite
([[sabotage-attribution-names-the-test]]), so it was redone as a bounded block swap with an
`ast.parse` check. Both restores sha256-verified to `bb9c1cb7…`, sabotage runs under
`python -B` ([[sabotage-restores-masked-by-pycache]]). `ruff@0.15.15` + `black@25.11.0` clean.
**Decisions.** None pinned; no threshold or gate semantics moved. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); the feature-branch
commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 6) — 2026-07-31: an ADR-signed population that nothing enforced, and a wording change refused

**Inputs.** `coderabbit review --agent -t committed --base main` over `6c7859a`. Two findings,
one real. **Process.** The real one: the twin's publish guard checked
`n_gate4_eval_excluded > 0`, and a positive count cannot tell **1,204** from 900. Reading the
governing text rather than the roadmap's paraphrase ([[convenience-is-not-a-prd-argument]]),
ADR-0004 **A6 pins the graded population by measurement**, not by its carve rule alone —
"1,201 records / 1,029 clusters / 154 genera / 15 orders / 2,976,259 nt", and the twin carve
"8,303 → 7,099" withholding 1,204 records in 1,031 clusters — and **nothing in the repo
enforced a single one of those numbers**. Every clause that did exist is rule-shaped and a
drifted split table satisfies all of them: a re-clustered or re-drawn `fold_random` yields a
different population that is still `gate4_eval`, still disjoint from the twin, still
block-resamplable, and its GATE-4 number would look exactly like the signed one.

**Outputs.** Six A6 constants single-sourced in `window_dataset` beside the loader that owns
the population, and checked in three places: `gate4_eval_problems` gains a
**`population drift`** clause on records × clusters — which `compute_gate4` calls *before any
forward pass*, so a drifted population can never be graded at all; `gate4_problems` pins the
twin's `n_gate4_eval_excluded` / `n_gate4_eval_clusters` / `n_training_records` and the gated
`n_positions` (the same record count over a different nucleotide extent is a different
measurement); and the sbatch's pre-publish guard refuses the same three, so a drifted twin's
checkpoint is never published. Changing the graded population is an ADR-0004 amendment
(§7 item 2) — these constants are where that becomes mechanical rather than aspirational.

**The second finding is refused, and the reasoning lives here.** It asked to reword the
`delta_governance` sentence so "0 of the 9" reads "0 of the 9 depositions", **and to regenerate
the report to match**. The sentence already opens "C is NOT estimable from these depositions",
so the referent is not ambiguous, and the fallback branch ("0 of the depositions supplied") is
already grammatical. Re-running a completed grade to change prose would put a freshly-generated
`generated_at_utc` on a measurement nothing about the science moved; editing the code without
re-running would leave the committed artifact one wording behind its generator, which is worse
than the wording. Neither is worth it, so nothing changed.

**Validation.** 105/105 standalone (was 98). **Seven further source-sabotage bites, each RED by
name:** neutering the drift clause reds the two `population drift` cases, the twin-pin loop reds
all four `pins it at …` cases, and the `n_positions` pin reds `different nucleotide`. Restores
sha256-verified (`a5bb45e4…`, `b5c067fb…`) under `python -B`. One case is worth recording: with
the drift clause disabled, `scope.n_blocks = 1028` is caught only by the CI-vs-scope block
mismatch, which fires solely because the CI block count stayed 1029 — a *consistently* drifted
run would trip nothing. The clause is not redundant with it. The sbatch's publish guard was
validated by extracting its heredoc and `ast.parse`-ing the shipped bytes, then driving it
against the **real** committed twin report (all three pins satisfied); `bash -n` clean;
`test_train_production_signals.py` + `test_sbatch_overrides.py` 9 passed / 1 skipped;
`ruff@0.15.15` over `src/` + `tests/` and `black@25.11.0` clean. The neighbouring suites that
touch the changed validator were run too, and their failures are harness artefacts (my
stub-`pytest` supplies no `tmp_path`/`pd` fixtures and stubs `approx` as identity) — **identical
counts before and after the change**, confirmed by stashing the edits and re-running.
**Decisions.** No pinned value moves; A6's numbers are enforced, not chosen. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); the
feature-branch commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 7) — 2026-07-31: the last cost knob, and two copies of a pinned number

**Inputs.** `coderabbit review --agent -t committed --base main` over `390f7ad`. Two findings,
both minor, both real. **Process + outputs.** **(1)** The r5 clauses closed `--max-records`,
`--loo-max-records` and `--no-loo`, but not `--n-boot`: a `--n-boot 50` run produces a far
noisier interval that is **not** the ADR-0005 D5 estimator and, at the phase-exit path, reads
exactly like the shipped one — the same shape of defect, one knob over. `--window` / `--stride`
are worse in kind, since re-tiling changes the reconciliation the frozen ADR-0005 D3+A3
operator is *defined* over. `gate4_problems` now pins the whole `geometry` block to
`(WINDOW_NT, STRIDE_NT, DEFAULT_N_BOOT)` = 1024/512/2000, rejecting missing and malformed as
well as mismatched. **(2)** My own r6 fix retyped `1204` / `1031` / `7099` into the sbatch
guard rather than importing them — exactly the two-copies-of-a-pinned-number shape that means
one gets amended and the other ships the old value
([[promote-dont-duplicate-is-a-correctness-rule]]). The guard now imports the three constants
from `window_dataset`, so `window_dataset` is the single source and an A6 amendment cannot
leave the cluster-side guard behind.

**Validation.** 109/109 standalone (was 105). Four further sabotage cases, and neutering the
geometry clause reds all four by name (`not the ADR-0005 D5 estimator`, `frozen scan geometry`
×3); restore sha256-verified (`6f6b5481…`). The sbatch guard was not merely re-read: its
heredoc was extracted and **executed as its own bytes** ([[verify-the-line-you-ship]]) under
`PYTHONPATH=src` in `tbox-ml-dna` — against the real committed twin report it prints
`twin-ok fold_scope=gate4_twin_train n_gate4_eval_excluded=1204 n_records=7099` and exits 0,
and against a report with `n_gate4_eval_excluded` set to 900 it exits **1** naming the pin. A
guard that only passes is not evidence; the designed control that must fire is
([[namespace-mismatch-invisible-noop]]). `bash -n` clean; `ruff@0.15.15` and `black@25.11.0`
clean over `src/` + `tests/` (190 files). **Decisions.** None; no pinned value moves.
**Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); feature-branch commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 8) — 2026-07-31: a helper that matched the wrong line, and a suggestion that was wrong about why

**Inputs.** `coderabbit review --agent -t committed --base main` over `69ca8eb`. Two findings,
both on `test_train_production_signals.py` — a *pre-existing* file this step did not author,
and both real. **Process.** The first: `_first_executable_line` skipped whole-line comments but
not **trailing** ones, so `_first_executable_line(sb.path, "torchrun")` matched
`export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2   # 16 cpus / 8 ranks; torchrun warns…` at line **207** rather than
the invocation at **241**. The restore-precedes-training assertion then held for the wrong
reason, and would have false-alarmed on a restore legitimately placed between the two.

**The suggested fix was wrong about the mechanism, and taking it would have broken the test.**
CodeRabbit proposed matching lines that *start with* the command. The real invocation is
`PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONPATH=src torchrun --standalone …`, so `startswith("torchrun")` finds
**nothing**, `train` becomes `None`, and the ordering assertion collapses. The defect is the
trailing comment, not the substring match, so the fix is a quote-aware
`_strip_inline_comment` — quote-aware because a bare `split("#")` would truncate at a `#`
inside a quoted string and silently shorten the text being matched.

The second: the run-signal assertions compared **basenames**, because the signals are written
as `"$OUT_DIR/train_stage1_gate4_twin.DONE"` and no whole path appears literally. That has a
genuine blind spot — the `.gitignore` rules for these signals are **path-anchored**
(`/reports/p2/…`), so re-pointing `OUT_DIR` moves every signal out from under its ignore rule
while the basenames, and the test, stay identical. `_expand_shell_vars` resolves the sbatch's
own `VAR="literal"` assignments so the registry is compared as whole paths, the way the
`--output`/`--error` directives already were.

**Validation.** 14 passed on the file (was 9): five new tests for the two **helpers
themselves** — the trailing-comment case by line number, the env-prefixed invocation a prefix
match would miss, a `#` inside quotes, the `$OUT_DIR` expansion *and* the blind spot it closes,
and `$SLURM_JOB_ID` surviving with no assignment to resolve. A helper that quietly matches the
wrong line makes every assertion above it weaker than it reads, and the way that stays
invisible is never testing the helper ([[tests-can-specify-the-bug]]). **Sabotage:** re-pointing
`OUT_DIR` from `reports/p2` to `logs/p2` in the shipped sbatch reds
`test_the_run_signal_paths_are_the_ones_the_sbatch_actually_writes` — which the basename version
passed — restore sha256-verified (`7a465b65…`). `ruff@0.15.15` caught a real defect in my own
first draft (B023: the substitution lambda closed over the loop variable `env`, so every pass
would have substituted from whichever dict the loop ended on); fixed by passing `env` as a
parameter. `ruff` + `black@25.11.0` clean over `src/` + `tests/` (190 files). **Decisions.**
None. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); feature-branch commit on `p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-14 (CodeRabbit round 9) — 2026-07-31: one finding, refuted by execution; the review converges

**Inputs.** `coderabbit review --agent -t committed --base main` over `c9651d1`. One finding,
major, **refuted**. **Process.** It read the twin's training report — `eval_requested: false`,
`warm_start: null`, yet `gate.eval_val_scored_on_disjoint_fold: true` and
`gate.warm_start_loaded: true` — and inferred the two clauses "default to true" when the
evidence is absent. That is the right suspicion to have here: it is the
[[clauses-must-guard-emptiness]] shape that cost this project ~20 GPU-h once and produced a
green P2-05 gate resting on zero measurements. It is also, in this instance, wrong — and the
way to establish that is to run the clauses, not to read their docstrings.

Both absence branches **require the absence to be recorded and coherent**, not merely
unviolated: `_eval_val_ok` returns `requested is False and metrics_block is None and scope is
None`, and `_warm_start_ok` requires a fresh build to *say so* and cross-checks the run config.
Five designed controls, every one of which would stay TRUE under the alleged defect, all return
**False**: an `eval_requested: false` report that nonetheless claims `eval_metrics`; one that
claims an `eval_scope`; an `eval_requested` that is absent rather than explicitly `False`; an
`eval_requested: true` with the scope missing; and a `warm_start` block claimed with no
`init_from_checkpoint` in the config. The clauses were hardened into this shape by P2-06a and
P2-10d and their docstrings carry the reasoning; nothing was changed.

Worth recording for the next reader: these clauses do not gate GATE-4 in any case.
`eval/gate4.py` reads the training report's `class_counts_scope` and the provenance sha256 —
never `report["gate"]` — so the twin's internal self-certification and the GATE-4 verdict are
independent chains.

**Nine rounds, and this is the convergence point.** r5–r8 each found something real and each
was fixed; r9's only finding does not survive execution. The findings also migrated outward
over the rounds — from the deliverable's own certification (r5), to the ADR pins behind it
(r6, r7), to helper strictness in a pre-existing test file (r8), to a refuted reading of a
pre-existing trainer clause (r9) — which is what convergence looks like. **Validation.** No
code changed this round; the refutation is the artifact. **Commit.** squash **`3b13222`** on `main` (PR [#91](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/91)); feature-branch commit on
`p2-14-gate4`.

## Step P2-15 — 2026-07-31: the Phase-2 exit gate — the dev-log's own provenance was the defect

**Inputs.** The eleven Phase-2 artifact families this phase produced: three DVC-tracked Stage-1
checkpoints (`stage1_production`, `stage1_classII_naive`, `stage1_gate4_twin`) each with its own
`provenance.json`; `reports/p2/{gate4,ablation_table,calibration,sweep_selection,tier2n_probe,`
`classII_recovery,mine_round_measure,train_stage1_*}.json`; the 80 accumulated stanzas of this
file; `README.md`; `paper/manuscript.qmd`; ADR-0002/0004/0005.

**Process.** Prose + release-doc only — **no `src/`, no test, no `.smk`, no data change.**
(1) **Checkpoint provenance verified, not regenerated.** All three `provenance.json` already carry
rule, script path, git SHA, env-lock hash, seed, and input/output SHA-256s (PRD §11); the naive
one was read out of the DVC cache rather than materialised, so nothing was re-run and no
`git_sha` drifted ([[dvc-artifact-worktree-rematerialize]]). (2) **Phase-gate `dvc push`** to the
cluster-scratch remote, capacity pre-verified first per PRD §15 — `/onedata` shows **30 TB free**
against a 25 GB local cache, so the gate is cleared by ~3 orders of magnitude, not by assertion.
(3) **`docs/model_card.md`** drafted: the PRD §10.1 **two-run split** and **per-checkpoint GATE
attribution** are its §2, stated as a three-row table because Phase 2 produced *three* artifacts,
not two — the eval twin is a checkpoint a reader can otherwise mistake for the shipped one.
(4) **README + manuscript**: the Phase-2 headline now leads with GATE-4 and carries the ~0.72
across-order number in the same breath; a **Figure 2** caption was added to `@sec-gate4`
(the §6.2 manuscript paragraph itself landed with P2-14). (5) **Phase-2-exit cross-reference
bullets** appended to ADR-0002/0004/0005 — no pinned value moved in any of them.

**The defect this step existed to catch.** Rendering the phase log to PDF is where dangling
provenance becomes visible, and this file's was **comprehensively** dangling. Of the 79 stanzas
this phase accumulated, 76 carried a `Commit.` pointer (78 lines in all — P2-10c′-c-ii carries
three), and **every one of the 78 fails to resolve from `main`** — explicit placeholders
(`<SHA — reconcile against git log main at the P2 exit gate>`, `SHA pending`, `squash pending`),
or the subtler `this stanza's commit on <branch>`, which reads like a record but names a
feature-branch commit that squash-merging discarded. Three further stanzas (P2-06 result,
P2-10d′-c, P2-10d′-e) carried **no** `Commit.` line at all. This is the same class of defect the
P1 exit gate found and fixed, recurring because every stanza is written before its own squash
exists. All 81 pointers (78 rewritten + 3 inserted) now read
`squash **<sha>** on main (PR #N)`, and every mapping was **derived, not recalled**: for each
candidate squash commit, `git show <sha> -- analyses/phase2_log.qmd | grep '^+## Step'` names the
stanzas that commit actually introduced. That check caught a real mis-assignment on the first
pass — a prefix-matching rule bound both `P2-10c′-fetch` stanzas to `bac19ad` (#78, the
held-out-order-negative step) because `P2-10c′-f` is a prefix of `P2-10c′-fetch`; the correct
squash is `b3624f1` (#80). An earlier whole-stanza rewrite also silently absorbed a blockquote
and two trailing paragraphs into the `Commit.` sentence; it was reverted and redone line-scoped,
so the rewrite is line-for-line and the only added lines are the three insertions.

**Validation.** **GATE-4 documented**: 0.951776 vs the 0.80 floor, CI [0.9426, 0.9605], reaching
`README.md`, `paper/manuscript.qmd` §sec-gate4 + Figure 2, `docs/model_card.md` §5, and the three
ADR bullets — every restatement re-read from `reports/p2/gate4.json`, never retyped from a
summary ([[size-a-run-from-the-protocols-own-report]]). DVC remote capacity confirmed **before**
the push. 81/81 `Commit.` pointers resolve. CI green (`ruff`/`black`, `snakemake --lint`/`-n`,
`pytest tests/{unit,golden,ml}` incl. the no-leakage and eval-gate tests).

**The exit-gate item that is NOT met.** The P2 checklist line *"hard-negative-mining loop executed
with the non-canonical spare rule"* is **unmet**, and is disclosed rather than ticked. The loop is
machinery-complete, certified, and measured (N₀ = 941 FPs / 660 genomes), but only 1 of its 3
spare-rule evidence disjuncts has a backend, the rule fails closed, and a round is therefore a
verified structural no-op ([[p2-spare-rule-spares-everything]]). The deferral is a recorded §7
decision of 2026-07-28, not a silent waiver — it is stated in `docs/model_card.md` §8, in the
ADR-0005 Phase-2-exit bullet, and in the `README.md` headline. Every other checklist item is met
and evidenced by a committed artifact.

**Decisions.** No ADR amendment and no new sign-off: the three cross-reference bullets record
where Phase-2 work touched each ADR and change no decision or value (CLAUDE.md §6.4 update
reflex, not §7 item 2). The render-command comment at the head of this file was corrected from
the laptop directory name `tbox-finder-viz` to the **committed** env name `tbox-viz`
(`envs/viz.yml`) — the identical P0-exit `/ultrareview` finding, recurring
([[env-name-committed-vs-laptop]]); a fresh clone has only the committed name. Figure 2 follows
the established `#fig-splits` pattern (caption + render-time placeholder image) rather than
introducing a generated PNG, which would need its own provenance chain and is out of this step's
scope. §10.1 N/A — this step asserts no new biological or statistical fact; every number is
re-read from a committed report.

**Commit.** squash SHA + PR recorded at the P2-15 merge; feature-branch commit on `p2-15-exit`.

## Step P2-15 (ultrareview round) — 2026-07-31: a caption that reordered its own referents

**Inputs.** The cloud `/ultrareview` of PR [#92](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/92)
(user-triggered — CLAUDE.md §11). **One** finding, severity nit, **valid and applied**.

**Process.** The Figure 2 caption enumerated the left panel's core elements in one order —
`Stem I 0.975, Antiterminator 0.970, Specifier 0.952`, descending-numeric *for that panel* — and
then gave the right panel as bare `0.765 / 0.721 / 0.715`. The across-order triple is also
descending-numeric, but its rank order is **different**: Antiterminator 0.7646, Stem I 0.7214,
Specifier 0.7154 (`reports/p2/gate4.json` → `loo_holdout.macro_per_element_f1`). A reader applying
the same-order-within-a-caption convention therefore gets Stem I = 0.765 and Antiterminator =
0.721 — the top two inverted, reading Stem I as the LOO-strongest core element when it is the
second-weakest of the three. The values were right; the labelling was not. Captions are read
standalone, and the labelled ground truth living one paragraph above (manuscript:216) and in
`docs/model_card.md` §5.2 does not rescue a caption cited on its own. Fixed by relabelling the
right-panel numbers in the same explicit style used everywhere else, plus a clause saying *why*
the labels are there — the rank order genuinely differs between panels, which is itself part of
the finding rather than a formatting accident. No number changed.

**Validation.** Re-read the three LOO values from `reports/p2/gate4.json` before editing rather
than copying the reviewer's quotation ([[size-a-run-from-the-protocols-own-report]]) — they match.
Manuscript re-rendered clean, `@fig-gate4` still resolves to "Figure 2"; this dev-log re-rendered
to `docs/dev-log/phase2_2026-07-31.pdf` so the committed PDF carries this stanza. CI green.

**Decisions.** None pinned; no threshold, gate, ADR, or committed metric moved — this is a
labelling fix inside a draft manuscript whose submission gate is Phase 7. `README.md` and
`docs/model_card.md` were checked for the same positional-ambiguity shape: the model card §5.2
already labels every element, and the README quotes only the aggregate ~0.72, so neither needed
a change.

**Commit.** squash SHA + PR recorded at the P2-15 merge; feature-branch commit on `p2-15-exit`.
